/articles/how-agent-style-ordering-works.title: How LoloBuy Ordering Works
/articles/how-agent-style-ordering-works.description: Follow the LoloBuy ordering workflow from product link and variant notes to warehouse arrival, QC decisions and parcel submission.
/articles/how-agent-style-ordering-works.body:
Agent-style shopping separates the product order from international parcel shipping. Understanding those stages helps you keep the correct link, variant and evidence together instead of treating one product card as a complete purchase.

1. Start with the exact product route

Open the product card and confirm that the destination matches the item you intended to view. Compare the product image, title, seller information, available variants and item identifier. Generic titles are common, so use several matching details rather than relying on a single word.

Before submitting an order, record the original link, item ID, chosen color, size, version and quantity. If the listing offers several similar variants, save the precise selection in your notes. A screenshot can preserve visible details if the seller later edits the listing, but the live checkout remains the final source for price and availability.

2. Review the order before warehouse arrival

The displayed item price is not the full delivered cost. Domestic delivery, optional services, payment conversion and international shipping may appear at different stages. Keep the original currency beside any USD estimate and verify the payable amount before confirmation.

After ordering, monitor the current order status. Do not assume every seller uses the same dispatch speed or accepts the same after-sales request. If a product is delayed, changed or unavailable, use the actions shown for that specific order.

3. Match the warehouse arrival to your selection

When the item arrives, compare the warehouse record with your saved selection. Check product type, color, quantity, version and visible size label. Warehouse photos are evidence for this decision; they are not decoration. If an important detail is missing, request a focused image or measurement only when that option is available.

4. Make a clear QC decision

Classify each item as accepted, needs clarification or action required. Check overall shape, visible construction, print or embroidery placement, stitching, hardware, labels, packaging and measurements that matter for the category. Only accepted items should move into the parcel plan.

5. Build the parcel with current data

Once the selected items are ready, review actual weight, dimensions, item type and available routes. Consolidation can reduce repeated base charges, but a larger box can also increase volumetric weight. Group items by compatibility, not only by arrival date, and compare the current checkout conditions before submitting the parcel.

Final ordering checklist

  • Product destination and variant match the intended item.
  • Original link, item ID and selection are recorded.
  • Warehouse arrival matches the order notes.
  • QC questions are resolved before parcel submission.
  • Only accepted items are grouped.
  • Current route, weight, dimensions and final cost are reviewed.
Independent guide: Always verify the live product, order, warehouse and parcel pages before paying because availability, services, routes and fees can change.

Use a three-record order trail

Keep a source record, a received-item record and a parcel record. The first stores the original product link, source ID and selected variant. The second stores what arrived and the inspection decision. The third stores the accepted items selected for shipping, packaging choices and current route quote. A change to one record should not silently overwrite another.

For example, if a seller substitutes a different colour, update the order decision before approving warehouse photos. If you later request another size, check that replacement independently. A previous approval is evidence about the earlier item, not every item sharing its title.

Recover from an unclear product link

Use the product-link finder to match known source IDs to the existing catalogue. When a source is unknown, search the name or ID and compare the result. Do not turn an external marketplace ID into a catalogue path without an established mapping.

product-link finder

For footwear, use the shoe measurement guide. For clothing, compare the garment measurements before relying on a size letter. Save unresolved questions so that checkout does not become an accidental approval.

shoe measurement guide · garment measurements

Keep the next action visible

Each item needs one next action: waiting for seller information, awaiting arrival, checking evidence, requesting an available correction or ready for a parcel. Note the date and the reason. This makes a multi-seller order easier to review than a single generic “in progress” status. Use the current account terms for all deadlines.

/articles/lolobuy-coupons-exchange-rate-.title: LoloBuy Coupons and Exchange Rates: Check the Final Cost
/articles/lolobuy-coupons-exchange-rate-.description: Check LoloBuy coupon conditions, failed discounts, currency conversion and final checkout totals. Includes a practical savings example.
/articles/lolobuy-coupons-exchange-rate-.body:
A coupon or converted spreadsheet price is only one part of the final order total. Use the current checkout to confirm eligibility, conversion and payable amount before making a decision.

Planning rule: Treat every displayed discount and converted price as provisional until the current checkout applies it to the exact order, route and destination.

Separate product price from the complete cost

A product listing may show the seller price while other costs appear later. Depending on the order, domestic delivery, optional warehouse services, payment conversion and international parcel charges may be separate. Keep these categories distinct in a spreadsheet so a low item price is not mistaken for a low delivered cost.

Check coupon scope and eligibility

Coupons can be limited by date, minimum spend, account status, product, service or route. A promotional value displayed on one page does not prove it will apply to every item or parcel. Add the coupon at the relevant checkout stage and confirm that the payable total actually changes. Avoid counting multiple discounts together unless the current interface shows they can be combined.

If a discount disappears, review the active dates, threshold, currency, eligible service and whether another promotion replaced it. The practical evidence is the final order summary, not a social post or an older buyer screenshot.

Understand currency conversion

A USD value on this site is an estimate for comparison. The payment provider or platform may use a different live rate and may include a conversion or transaction cost. Small differences become more noticeable across several items, so keep the original currency beside every converted estimate.

For planning, record the original amount, the date of the estimate and the converted amount. At payment, compare that estimate with the actual charge shown before confirmation. Do not use a fixed historical rate as a promise of the final total.

Recheck the parcel stage

Product coupons and international shipping discounts may apply at different stages. A discount on the item order does not automatically reduce the later parcel charge. At parcel checkout, confirm route eligibility, weight or spending thresholds, expiry and the final amount after the discount.

Simple cost record

  • Original product price and currency
  • Domestic delivery shown for the order
  • Optional service charges selected
  • Coupon entered and actual reduction applied
  • Payment conversion shown before confirmation
  • Final parcel weight, dimensions and route quote
  • International shipping discount actually applied

Save the final totals rather than only the advertised coupon values. That gives you a reliable comparison for future orders without presenting a temporary promotion or exchange rate as a permanent fact.

Record an applied discount, not an advertised headline

This page does not list a verified live coupon code. A code should only be called working after its current conditions and actual checkout effect have been checked. Record the code, expiry, eligible service, minimum spend and the reduction shown for your exact transaction. A historical screenshot or signup headline is not enough.

If a code does not apply, check whether it belongs to product payment or international shipping, whether a threshold is met, whether the service is eligible and whether another offer prevents combining it. Use the wording displayed in the current checkout. Do not create extra accounts or orders simply to test assumptions about eligibility.

Compare before-and-after totals in the same currency

Consider an illustrative $80 eligible charge with a $5 reduction, giving $75 for that charge. If another $3 service remains payable, the total for those two components is $78. The discount has not eliminated the separate service. These figures are hypothetical and do not describe a current LoloBuy promotion.

Likewise, a converted USD price can differ from the actual payment amount. Keep the original currency, applied exchange rate and any separately disclosed transaction charge together. The currency conversion guide explains how to compare the same basket consistently.

currency conversion guide

Choose savings that still suit the order

Adding an unwanted item to reach a coupon threshold can raise the total basket and parcel cost. Compare the complete cost with and without that item, including its shipping effect. A larger advertised saving is not useful if the final amount paid for what you need increases.

Continue with the payment-fee checklist and total-cost worksheet. Keep the accepted final summary so that the comparison uses evidence from the actual transaction.

/articles/lolobuy-hoodie-finds-size-char.title: LoloBuy Hoodie Finds: Size Charts, Measurements and QC
/articles/lolobuy-hoodie-finds-size-char.description: Use garment measurements, clear product links and QC checks to compare LoloBuy hoodie finds and plan clothing shipping.
/articles/lolobuy-hoodie-finds-size-char.body:
LoloBuy hoodie finds are easier to compare when you begin with the garment you want to wear, rather than a letter on a size label. An oversized sweatshirt, a cropped hoodie and a regular zip-up can all be described as size L while fitting very differently. A useful clothing spreadsheet therefore needs measurements, construction details and a parcel plan alongside its product links.

This guide shows how to build that record, review the available QC photographs and decide which uncertainties matter before shipping. It does not claim that a particular hoodie has been worn or tested. LoloBuy's official app description establishes its stated role in Chinese-product shopping and international delivery; individual garment specifications must come from the actual listing and the evidence available for your order.

Choose the silhouette before the size

Take a hoodie you already enjoy wearing and lay it flat without stretching the fabric. Measure its chest width, body length and sleeve length, using a consistent starting point each time. Record whether the shoulder is dropped, whether the hem is cropped and whether the fit includes room for a layer underneath. Those details explain your preference better than writing “usually medium.”

Compare those measurements with the seller's chart for the exact item. Check whether chest means flat width or full circumference, whether body length begins at the shoulder or collar, and whether sleeve length includes the shoulder. A number is only comparable when the measurement method matches. If a chart's diagram is unclear, resolve that before choosing a size.

Do not use one universal size-up rule across all LoloBuy clothing finds. Some garments intentionally have broad shoulders and short bodies; others are narrow and long. Choosing a larger size may increase length without creating the shape you want. Write the intended silhouette into your shortlist so that a visually different garment is not accepted merely because the label matches.

Build a clothing row that answers practical questions

Keep the product link, source item ID, selected colour and size together. Add the observed price and currency, the date you recorded it, the seller's measurement chart and your comparison measurements. Save the original selection before checkout, especially where several designs share one product page.

The finds page includes existing sweatshirt catalogue entries associated with source IDs 7765045446 and 7755070499. Use them to begin checking current options rather than assuming that either entry is a verified hoodie recommendation. A sweatshirt may not have a hood, and a product title alone may not describe every available variant. The live picture, option and measurements must agree.

finds page

Keep unknown fields visible. If fabric composition is not shown, write “not confirmed.” If the available weight includes packaging, label it accordingly. An incomplete but honest row is more useful than guessed cotton percentages, warmth ratings or precise weights. Do not copy those details from a similar-looking garment sold by somebody else.

Read fabric and construction claims carefully

A photograph can reveal visible texture, seam placement, print position and some finishing details. It cannot reliably establish fibre composition, fabric weight per square metre, colourfastness or how the garment will feel after washing. A composition label is a claim attached to the garment, not an independent laboratory result.

Where fabric weight is stated, establish what the number measures. Total garment weight and fabric density are different quantities. A heavier hoodie may have a larger size, a lined hood, metal hardware or thicker packaging. Comparing two total weights without those details can lead to an inaccurate conclusion about fabric quality.

For a zip-up, look for the zipper sitting straight and for obvious misalignment where the design crosses the opening. For a pullover, inspect the neckline, hood attachment, cuffs and hem. If durability is important, visible stitching is one useful clue, but photographs cannot predict how a seam or print will perform over time.

Turn QC photographs into a measurement check

Begin by matching the received garment to the order: design, colour, size label and quantity. Then review the overall front and back before zooming into details. This prevents a close-up of a neat logo from distracting you from a wrong colour, missing feature or noticeably different cut.

If measurement photographs are available, request a specific view with the garment flat and the ruler visible from the correct starting point. Compare the result with both the seller chart and your reference hoodie. Do not treat a folded garment or a diagonal tape as a precise measurement. Ask for clarification when the method makes the number ambiguous.

Keep your tolerance decision personal and explicit. A small difference might be acceptable in a relaxed layer but important in a cropped fit or close neckline. Do not present your preference as a universal manufacturing tolerance. Record the measurement, the uncertainty and whether it still meets your intended fit.

A practical comparison of two sizes

Imagine a reference hoodie with a flat chest width of 60 cm and a body length of 68 cm. One hypothetical listing offers a size with a 60 cm chest and 64 cm length, and another with a 63 cm chest and 68 cm length. Neither is automatically the correct choice. The first may be too short for your purpose, while the second may be wider than you want.

Decide which dimension is essential, then consider the shoulder and sleeve construction. A dropped shoulder can change how sleeve length feels even when the chart number looks familiar. If neither option suits the desired silhouette, choosing another listing may be better than buying the nearest letter size.

These measurements are an illustrative comparison, not a chart for a real product. Replace them with the live listing's numbers and your own garment measurements. The exercise is useful because it forces a decision about fit before international postage makes a correction more inconvenient.

Plan hoodie shipping without guessing weight

Clothing can compress, but compression does not remove its actual weight. The effect on shipping depends on the packed parcel, the selected service and its billing rules. A bulky hood, multiple layers or retail packaging may affect volume, while several dense garments can still form a heavy parcel.

If a packing option is available, consider creasing, trims, zippers and any structured decoration before requesting compression. Do not assume every garment is suitable for the same handling. Confirm what the service will do and what it costs before including a saving in your budget.

Use the actual and volumetric weight guide to distinguish the two measurements, and the total-cost worksheet to keep item price separate from delivery. Compare complete parcel scenarios rather than allocating the same invented freight amount to every hoodie.

actual and volumetric weight guide · total-cost worksheet

Finish the shortlist with an actionable note

For each candidate, write one decision: ready to order, waiting for size information, awaiting QC clarification or removed from the shortlist. Include the reason. “Body length matches; sleeve method unclear” is useful on the next visit; “probably fine” is not. Keep a rejected item in your private notes if it helps avoid repeating the same research.

Before approving a received garment, confirm that the measurements you needed are recorded, visible defects have been addressed and any seller action is still available under the current terms. Do not assume storage time extends a return window. Finally, group accepted items with compatible packaging and review the current parcel quote.

Continue with the QC photo guide for inspection decisions, or the category directory for another clothing starting point. The goal is a smaller set of well-understood garments whose fit and shipping requirements you can explain before paying.

QC photo guide · category directory

Editorial basis: official LoloBuy app description checked 4 October 2026; existing catalogue entries are used only as discovery references. All numerical sizing examples are hypothetical. No fabric test, wear test, seller verification or current-stock guarantee is implied.

/articles/lolobuy-link-not-working.title: LoloBuy Link Not Working? Fix Taobao, Weidian & 1688 URLs
/articles/lolobuy-link-not-working.description: Fix LoloBuy product-link problems: check Taobao, Weidian and 1688 URLs, source listings, item IDs, manual ordering and imported options.
/articles/lolobuy-link-not-working.body:
A LoloBuy product link can fail because the source listing has changed, the copied address is incomplete, or the import has not recognised the item. Start with the original marketplace page, then compare what LoloBuy imports. Replacing random digits or ordering a similar-looking result can create a different problem: buying the wrong item.

Identify the stage that failed

Keep the original product address and the exact message shown on screen. Separate three stages: opening the source listing, importing its details into LoloBuy, and selecting an available variant. A page that loads but has no purchasable size is different from an address that never reaches a product. The correct next step depends on which stage actually failed.

Make one change at a time and note the result. If you simultaneously replace the link, switch the seller and change the colour, you cannot tell which change helped. Before paying, compare the final product with the item you originally wanted, even when a retry appears successful.

Copy a complete source product link

Open the listing from the marketplace or from the original seller reference. Copy the product address after the page has loaded. A share message can contain marketing text, an app invitation or a shortened redirect alongside the actual link. Paste the address itself, without the surrounding sentence. Do not paste account, payment or private order pages into a public search box.

For a Weidian listing, the item identifier commonly appears in the itemID query field. Taobao and Tmall product addresses commonly use an id field. An ordinary 1688 product address contains an offer number in its path. Preserve the original marketplace host and the complete identifier. These patterns help you recognise a listing; they do not prove that the seller still offers it.

When a short address opens successfully, copy the resulting product page rather than guessing its destination. If it only opens an app, use the marketplace's available sharing or browser option to obtain a product reference. Do not guess an identifier from a screenshot or remove every query field: some fields identify the actual item.

Check whether the source listing is still available

Try the original listing separately from LoloBuy. Look for a removed item, a seller notice, unavailable variants or a sign-in requirement. A sign-in screen alone does not prove that the listing has been deleted. Equally, an old spreadsheet image does not prove that stock remains available today. Record what the source actually displays.

If the listing has been removed, ask the seller or use a new verified source. A replacement link needs a fresh comparison of seller, product photographs, specifications, price and available options. Similar pictures can appear across different sellers and versions. Treat a replacement as a new purchase decision, rather than assuming that it inherits the old item's reviews or QC evidence.

Separate an import problem from missing stock

If the original source works but LoloBuy does not populate the product details, preserve both addresses and the import message. Reopen the product through LoloBuy's current entry point and check whether the source URL has been copied completely. A blank image, an error notice and an unavailable option are different observations; include the specific one when asking for help.

Do not submit duplicate paid orders while testing the same link. Review the cart and order history after a successful retry. If an earlier attempt created an order, resolve that record before paying again. A working import only establishes that details were retrieved; it does not guarantee seller stock, acceptance of your requested option or a particular delivery date.

Use manual ordering only with complete specifications

LoloBuy's public manual-entry form requests the product link, product name, specifications, price, freight to the warehouse and quantity. When the current platform offers this route, prepare the exact colour, size, version and quantity, together with a source screenshot that shows the intended option. Keep the original currency and distinguish the item price from domestic freight.

The manual-entry page warns that some third-party purchases may carry additional fees or different return conditions and may be impossible to order. Confirm the actual purchasing feedback before treating a manually entered request as accepted. Do not fill an unknown price with a token amount or assume that a successful form submission confirms the final payable total.

Write a short, precise specification instead of a vague instruction such as “the usual version.” For example, record the colour label exactly as shown, the seller's size label and the quantity. If you need a particular measurement, request confirmation before purchase rather than adding a contradictory note after the order is underway.

Understand what the product-link finder can resolve

The LoloBuyChina product-link finder matches recognised source identifiers to existing catalogue records. A marketplace item identifier and a catalogue record number are different things. For example, a known source can map to a shorter catalogue address; replacing that shorter number with the source identifier would invent a page.

LoloBuyChina product-link finder

If no established match exists, the finder opens a catalogue search. Search results are candidates, not a guarantee that the first card is your item. Compare the source ID, seller context, image and selected option. A keyword search is useful when a link is incomplete, but it cannot restore a deleted listing or confirm stock on behalf of a seller.

Save a useful support request

Send the original source URL, the LoloBuy page or relevant order reference, the exact visible error, the time of the attempt and the variant you want. State whether the source opens independently and whether the problem occurs before or after option selection. This makes it easier to distinguish a parsing issue from an unavailable product.

Use the official support channel for private order details. Crop unrelated account information from screenshots and avoid posting addresses, payment records or complete private tracking details in public. Keep a copy of the response with your product notes. If support gives a replacement link, verify that replacement before continuing.

Complete the purchase check after the link works

Compare the imported title, seller reference, photographs, colour, size, quantity and current price with the source. Read any restrictions or after-sales conditions attached to the item. Confirm whether the displayed amount includes domestic freight and remember that international parcel shipping is a later cost. A repaired link does not make a historical spreadsheet price current.

Save the final selection and use it again when warehouse photos arrive. If the item differs, the original source record helps explain what was ordered. Continue with the QC inspection checklist before shipment. If a paid order needs to be stopped or an item returned, use the returns and refunds guide to organise the request around its current stage.

QC inspection checklist · returns and refunds guide

/articles/lolobuy-returns-refunds.title: LoloBuy Returns & Refunds: Cancel an Order and Track Your Refund
/articles/lolobuy-returns-refunds.description: Check LoloBuy cancellation, warehouse returns and refund records. Separate order stages, return costs, balance credits and payment-method refunds.
/articles/lolobuy-returns-refunds.body:
Start a LoloBuy cancellation or return request from the exact order and its current stage. An unpaid order, a seller purchase, an item stored in the warehouse and an international parcel require different checks. Keep the request, returned item and money movement as separate records so you can see what has actually been completed.

Record the current order stage before taking action

Open the relevant order and save its reference, selected variant, quantity, payment record and current status. Check whether purchasing has started, whether the seller has dispatched, whether warehouse inspection is available and whether the item has been included in a parcel. Use the wording visible in your account rather than assuming that an older tutorial has the same buttons.

Note what you want: cancellation before purchase, return of a received item, replacement with a different option, or clarification of a refund already approved. These are different requests. If several items share one payment, identify the item and quantity concerned so that a request for one product is not interpreted as a request about the whole order.

Distinguish cancellation from a warehouse return

For an unpaid order, first confirm that no payment or balance deduction was completed. Removing an unpaid request is not evidence that money has been refunded. For a paid order that has not yet been purchased, check the cancellation action available in the account and obtain confirmation that the purchasing process has stopped. Sending a message does not itself cancel an order.

If the seller has already dispatched, cancellation may involve a return rather than simply stopping a purchase. Ask which process applies to that item and whether any freight or handling remains payable. Do not submit a replacement order merely because the first request is pending; you could end up with two accepted purchases.

Inspect warehouse evidence promptly

When warehouse photos become available, compare the received item with your saved source link and selected option. Record a wrong colour, size label, quantity, missing accessory or visible defect precisely. Ask for a focused photograph or measurement when the available evidence cannot resolve the issue and that service is offered for the order.

Keep inspection decisions separate from parcel submission. If you are requesting a return, check whether the item can be held out of a parcel while the request is reviewed. Do not approve international dispatch of an unresolved item on the assumption that it can always be recalled later. Save the actual response confirming the item's status.

Verify the applicable return window and conditions

Read the current terms for the purchased item and the order's displayed deadline. Record the event from which any window runs, the relevant time zone and the last permitted action. A storage allowance is not a return allowance. Free warehouse storage does not mean that a seller will accept a return throughout the same period.

Seller conditions can differ by product, customisation and purchasing channel. LoloBuy's public manual-entry form specifically warns that some third-party purchases may not offer the same return or exchange service as ordinary marketplace orders. Do not assume that every listing is eligible or that a missing deadline means unlimited time.

This guide does not state a universal return deadline, refund processing time or guaranteed fee. If the account terms are unclear, ask support to confirm eligibility and the relevant deadline for the exact order. Retain that answer alongside the order record instead of relying on a promotional page or another buyer's experience.

Prepare an evidence-based request

Include the order reference, item identifier, selected variant, quantity, the reason for the request and the outcome you are seeking. Attach the source screenshot and the relevant warehouse image. Explain the difference concretely: a different labelled size, an absent component or a visible defect. Keep the original image so that a crop does not remove useful context.

For a sizing problem, distinguish a wrong delivered size from an item that matches the ordered label but does not fit your expectations. Include the seller's measurements and your requested measurement method when available. This distinction helps the service assess the request without implying that one explanation guarantees approval.

Use the official order or support channel to send private evidence. Public review pages are not a substitute for submitting the request within the applicable process. Keep a dated copy of the request and the reply, and follow the instructions actually given for that item.

Compare the refund amount with the full cost

Ask for the expected refund breakdown before accepting an optional paid return service. Keep the item amount, original domestic freight, return freight, service charges and any disclosed payment adjustment in separate fields. Whether each amount is recoverable depends on the transaction and the applicable conditions; a product refund should not automatically be treated as a refund of every cost.

Consider a hypothetical item costing 100 CNY with 10 CNY paid separately for domestic delivery. If an approved refund is 100 CNY and a further 12 CNY return cost remains payable, the result is not a recovery of the full 110 CNY originally spent. These are illustrative figures, not LoloBuy charges. Replace them with the amounts confirmed for your order.

For a partial return, record the quantity returned and the allocation shown in the actual refund record. Do not divide a combined payment equally between differently priced items unless that is how the platform describes the refund. Keep the original currency so that later conversion changes do not obscure the underlying amount.

Track the item movement and the refund separately

A return being approved, a parcel being sent back, a seller receiving it and a refund being recorded are separate events. Save the evidence available for each stage, including a return reference when provided. A tracking label marked delivered describes a package movement; it does not alone establish that a financial refund has been processed.

For the money record, note the approved amount, currency, destination and transaction reference. A credit appearing in the platform balance and money arriving at the original payment method are different outcomes. Read the actual refund destination before looking for a bank credit, and check any separate withdrawal process only if it is relevant and available to your account.

Follow up on a refund that remains unclear

Use the processing expectations supplied for your case. When following up, quote the request reference, approval date, confirmed amount and the last completed stage. Explain what is missing: return receipt confirmation, a refund transaction, a balance update or receipt by the payment provider. This is more useful than repeatedly asking whether the whole order is finished.

Preserve any new response and update the same timeline. Avoid creating multiple contradictory requests for the same item. If the recorded amount or destination differs from the approval, provide both records and ask for reconciliation. Do not label a refund lost merely because you checked the wrong account or payment destination.

Close the record before ordering a replacement

Confirm the outcome of the original item, any remaining charges and the refund destination. A replacement may need a new source check, current price, stock confirmation and fresh inspection. Review its measurements independently, even when the title and seller are unchanged. Keep the replacement order distinct from the returned item in your notes.

Use the tracking guide to separate domestic and international journeys, and the total-cost worksheet to reconcile the money. The QC checklist helps you record a clear decision before the next parcel is submitted.

tracking guide · total-cost worksheet · QC checklist

/articles/lolobuy-reviews-buyer-evidence.title: LoloBuy Reviews: How to Check Buyer Evidence Before Ordering
/articles/lolobuy-reviews-buyer-evidence.description: Read a dated LoloBuy review snapshot and learn to compare customer reports, shipping evidence and official claims before ordering.
/articles/lolobuy-reviews-buyer-evidence.body:
LoloBuy reviews can help you identify questions to ask before ordering, but a star score does not answer every buying decision. A smooth payment, a helpful support reply and a delivered parcel describe different outcomes. Reading them as if they prove the same thing can make a small collection of feedback seem much more conclusive than it is.

What the official records establish

The Google Play and Apple App Store listings identify LoloBuy as a cross-border shopping application from HONG KONG BEYOND TECHNOLOGY LIMITED. Their descriptions mention Chinese-product discovery and international shipping. Those records help identify the application being discussed. They do not independently certify delivery performance, individual sellers, product quality or a particular refund outcome.

An application update can show that software is being maintained, but a generic bug-fix note does not establish that a particular order problem was solved. Match any claimed improvement to a specific documented change. Avoid assuming that a new version guarantees lower shipping costs, faster dispatch or better inspection.

Identify the outcome a review actually covers

Classify a review by its furthest documented stage: browsing, payment, seller dispatch, warehouse receipt, inspection, parcel submission, international transport, delivery or after-sales resolution. A comment posted immediately after payment can describe checkout usability. It cannot yet demonstrate that the parcel arrived or that the clothing fit.

Then identify the part of the service being evaluated. A size problem may concern selection, an inaccurate seller chart, a received variant or a misunderstanding of measurements. A delivery problem may involve dispatch, the selected route, a carrier event or recipient instructions. Record the complaint without inventing which party caused it.

A detailed negative review can be useful even when its overall conclusion is overstated. A detailed positive review can be useful without establishing that every buyer should use the service. Extract the specific evidence and the practical question it raises. This approach avoids treating approval or criticism as an all-or-nothing verdict.

Look for comparable transaction details

  • Date: when the order and parcel events happened, not just when the review was posted.
  • Destination: the country and relevant delivery context, without exposing a private address.
  • Service: the route or service level used, where the reviewer provides it.
  • Parcel: the weight, dimensions or contents needed to understand a cost comparison.
  • Money: whether the figure is an estimate, a final charge or a refund claim.
  • Resolution: whether the issue remained open or was later addressed.

Do not require every public reviewer to publish sensitive information. A review can provide useful context without exposing order numbers or payment details. Equally, treat a missing field as unknown rather than filling it from another post. Different buyers may be discussing entirely different services under the same platform name.

Read review labels and incentives in context

Notice whether a platform labels a review as invited, verified or unprompted, but do not turn the label into your own guarantee. An invitation can affect who contributes. An unprompted post is also self-selected. A verification label should be interpreted according to that review platform's method, not as proof of every factual claim in the text.

Look for disclosed referral links, free products, credits or other benefits where relevant. Their presence does not automatically make the account false, but it can affect the incentives behind it. Their absence does not prove that no incentive exists. Keep the uncertainty visible and compare multiple accounts with meaningful details.

Repeated wording, identical photographs or several posts about the same transaction should not be counted as independent experiences. Conversely, do not accuse a reviewer of fabrication merely because a short comment resembles another short comment. Record patterns as reasons to seek stronger evidence, not as a basis for unsupported allegations.

Use Reddit discussions without losing the original context

A search for “LoloBuy Reddit” may return product showcases, referral promotions, preliminary impressions and completed-haul reports. Open the original discussion, check the date and read any later updates before relying on an excerpt. A search preview may omit a correction, a disclosure or a follow-up describing a different outcome.

Separate the product from the agent experience. A reviewer may like a pair of shoes while finding the shipping process confusing, or appreciate customer support while disliking the seller's sizing. Preserve both observations instead of reducing the post to a positive or negative vote. For a product choice, also compare the exact listing and variant.

Use public comments to develop a checklist for your own purchase. If a discussion raises measurement uncertainty, plan a measurement check. If it raises unclear parcel charges, record estimated and final figures separately. A review becomes more useful when it changes a specific action rather than simply making you more confident or worried.

Turn the evidence into a small, controlled decision

Before ordering, identify the uncertainty that would matter most to you: fit, seller availability, packaging, final cost or delivery timing. Check whether the available evidence addresses it. If it does not, seek the relevant information or reconsider the purchase. More general five-star comments cannot replace a missing size chart or a live parcel quote.

Keep the first comparison manageable. Record the exact product, selected options, expected costs and current service terms. Save the evidence available at each stage. This is a planning method, not a promise that a small order eliminates risk. Avoid adding more items merely to justify a quoted shipping amount before you understand how that quote was calculated.

Use our product-link guide to keep the correct source, the QC checklist to organise visible checks and the total-cost worksheet to record the budget. For a quiet tracking record, the tracking guide separates the relevant stages.

product-link guide · QC checklist · total-cost worksheet · tracking guide

A defensible decision is specific: you understand the item, the unresolved questions and the evidence you still need. The available public records can inform that decision, but they cannot justify a universal “safe,” “unsafe,” “best” or “guaranteed” label for every order.

/articles/lolobuy-shoe-finds-sizing-qc.title: LoloBuy Shoe Finds: Sizing, QC Photos and Product Links
/articles/lolobuy-shoe-finds-sizing-qc.description: Compare LoloBuy shoe finds using source IDs, sizing evidence, QC photos and packaging choices before building your parcel.
/articles/lolobuy-shoe-finds-sizing-qc.body:
A useful LoloBuy shoe find is a pair you can identify, size and budget for before you commit to international shipping. A thumbnail and a low advertised price do not answer those questions. This guide builds a practical shoe shortlist from product links, measurements, warehouse photographs and packaging choices. It is written for buyers comparing footwear through a spreadsheet, including anyone trying to avoid an inexpensive pair becoming an expensive parcel.

LoloBuy's official application listing describes a service for buying Chinese products and arranging international shipping. It does not establish the fit, authenticity, construction or sporting performance of an individual shoe. The checks below are independent buying guidance. Use the options and evidence available for your exact order; this article does not promise a particular inspection service, photo allowance or return window.

Start with an identifiable pair

Save the original marketplace link and the destination product page together. Record the item ID, selected colour, seller's size notation, quantity and any version option. Two listings can use the same promotional image while offering different variants. Likewise, two buttons labelled “42” may belong to different size charts. The details you submit matter more than the image that first caught your attention.

Our LoloBuy finds directory keeps the existing product destinations and reference images together. The footwear entries currently include source IDs 7777852466, 7711153142 and 7711145274. These are research starting points, not rankings or recommendations based on a physical test. Open the matching product record and recheck availability, variants and price before treating a saved row as an order.

LoloBuy finds directory

Give each candidate one clear purpose: everyday walking, an outfit, indoor casual use or a specific sport. Appearance does not prove suitability for running, basketball, work protection or medical support. If the decision depends on cushioning, slip resistance or impact protection, ordinary warehouse photographs cannot establish those properties. Seek appropriate product evidence before choosing that use.

Compare measurements rather than size labels alone

Measure both feet on a flat surface while standing, using the socks you expect to wear. Record the longer foot's length and note width or fit problems you already experience. Treat this as an input to the seller's chart, not a universal conversion formula. Do not automatically add a fixed amount or translate an EU number into a US number without checking the particular chart.

For a familiar comparison, measure a comfortable existing shoe where that measurement is meaningful. A removable insole can be easier to compare than an exterior sole, but an insole's total length is not the same as usable internal space. Toe shape, lining, heel structure and width still matter. Ask what the listing's measurement represents before relying on it.

A useful order note names the exact measurement: for example, the length of a removable insole photographed beside a ruler, if the seller or warehouse offers that service. A vague request for “check size” may produce only a size-label photograph. That label can verify what was received, but it cannot demonstrate that the shoe will fit your foot.

Review shoe QC in a repeatable order

  1. Identity: compare the pair, colour, version and size labels with the saved selection.
  2. Pair consistency: compare the left and right shoes from similar angles, checking obvious differences in shape or finish.
  3. Visible condition: inspect seams, glue marks, upper damage, hardware and exposed sole edges.
  4. Measurements: review any requested ruler photographs and check that the measurement method is clear.
  5. Contents: confirm the expected pair, accessories and packaging where they affect your decision.

Lighting and camera position can exaggerate a colour or shape difference. If one shoe looks wider, first compare photographs taken at matching angles. If a mark could be a shadow, request a focused view when available. Describe the exact area and the uncertainty you need resolved, rather than asking for a general set of extra images.

QC photographs are evidence of visible appearance at a particular stage. They do not verify authenticity, material composition, durability or long-term comfort. Avoid turning a clean photograph into an unsupported quality score. The QC review guide explains how to turn an observation into an accept, clarify or action-required decision.

QC review guide

Include the shoe box in the budget decision

A shoe box can protect shape and make storage or gifting easier, but it also occupies space. Removing it may reduce volume, yet the final saving depends on the packed dimensions, protection used instead and the charging rules of the selected route. Do not assume that every box removal produces a fixed discount.

Ask whether the proposed packaging protects the parts that matter: a structured toe, a stiff heel, delicate decoration or a light-coloured upper. A soft bag around a shape-sensitive pair may be a poor trade even if it reduces volume. Conversely, retaining several oversized boxes without measuring the final parcel can make an otherwise modest order costly.

Compare two recorded scenarios: keeping the original boxes and using suitable alternative protection. Use actual quotes if available; label estimates as estimates. Our parcel dimensions guide explains the measurements to record. The appropriate choice is the one that meets your protection needs at an acceptable delivered cost.

parcel dimensions guide

A worked shortlist without invented product promises

Consider two hypothetical pairs priced at $30 and $38. The cheaper pair has an unclear size chart and an unknown packed size; the other has measurements you can compare with a comfortable shoe. The $8 difference is only the starting point. Optional measurement services, domestic delivery, packaging and international freight can change the comparison.

Write both rows with the same fields: item price, original currency, selected size, measurement evidence, unresolved QC question, box choice and parcel estimate. Leave a field “unknown” when the information is missing. Assigning a confident number to an unknown cost makes the spreadsheet look complete while making the decision less reliable.

If one pair remains uncertain after reasonable checking, compare the cost of resolving that uncertainty with the cost of returning or not buying it. Do this before combining it with accepted items. The example does not describe real LoloBuy prices or a tested purchase; it illustrates a decision method that you can use with live figures.

Record a decision that survives the next visit

Use a short note such as “size label matches; width not confirmed; waiting for measurement” instead of “looks good.” A specific note tells you what remains unresolved when you return several days later. Keep the listing image separate from warehouse photographs so that a seller's promotional picture is never mistaken for evidence of your received pair.

When the pair is ready, save the accepted variant, the evidence reviewed and the packaging choice. If you change the order later, update those records too. A replacement size or colour needs its own check. Approval of the previous item should not silently carry over to a different pair.

Before parcel submission, confirm the pair is included once, the packaging request is recorded, the delivery address is correct and the current shipping quote is acceptable. Revisit the LoloBuy shipping guide for the parcel stage and the product-link guide if a saved destination no longer matches. A good shoe shortlist ends with a traceable decision, not a collection of appealing thumbnails.

LoloBuy shipping guide · product-link guide

Editorial basis: LoloBuy's Google Play application description, checked 4 October 2026, confirms its stated shopping and international-shipping purpose. Product examples retain this site's existing catalogue records; stock, fit, quality and live prices have not been independently certified. Measurement and comparison methods are editorial guidance.

/articles/lolobuy-tracking-order-status.title: LoloBuy Tracking Guide: Order Status and Parcel Updates
/articles/lolobuy-tracking-order-status.description: Understand LoloBuy order and parcel tracking, distinguish domestic delivery from international shipping, and investigate quiet updates.
/articles/lolobuy-tracking-order-status.body:
A LoloBuy tracking problem becomes easier to investigate once you identify which journey you are looking at. A seller sending an item to a warehouse is different from an international parcel travelling to your address. An order reference, a domestic courier number and a parcel tracking number can all appear during one purchase, but they do not describe the same movement.

This guide helps you build a clear status record and decide what to check next when tracking appears quiet. The stages below are descriptive categories, not a claimed list of exact LoloBuy interface labels. Read the wording in your current account and the selected carrier's record. No fixed dispatch time, delivery promise or compensation entitlement is assumed.

Separate the three records before troubleshooting

The product-order record identifies what you asked to buy: the source link, variant, quantity and payment state. Its progress can depend on seller stock, order clarification or dispatch. An order being paid does not itself establish that the seller has handed over a package, and a seller's dispatch notice does not mean that an international parcel exists.

The domestic-delivery record concerns the movement from the seller to the receiving warehouse. If several sellers are involved, each package may have its own number and delivery date. Keep them separate. One delivered package does not prove that every item in your planned haul has reached the warehouse.

The international-parcel record begins after the relevant stored items are selected and the parcel process is arranged. Its reference may differ from every domestic number. Save the route name, destination, parcel reference, carrier number where supplied, and the date of the last visible event. These fields let you ask about the correct package.

Use the last confirmed event as your starting point

Write down the event exactly as displayed and distinguish the event timestamp from the time you last opened the page. A translated label, an estimated delivery date and a physical carrier scan are different kinds of information. If the interface shows only a broad progress bar, look for a more detailed history before deciding that movement has stopped.

Check that the number belongs to the current parcel rather than an earlier test order or a domestic shipment. Copy it carefully, including any letters. If there is a carrier handoff, save both references when they are provided. Do not assume a new number means a new parcel, or that an unfamiliar number is automatically invalid.

Compare timestamps with their stated time zones. A scan late in one country can fall on the next calendar day in another. This usually matters when reconstructing a sequence or reporting a discrepancy, rather than when estimating a delivery date. Keep the original event text alongside your interpretation.

Work out which next action belongs to you

Before seller dispatch

Check whether the selected variant is available, whether the order needs clarification and whether any action is requested in the account. Ask about the exact item rather than the entire haul.

Domestic delivery

Match the courier number to the item and receiving destination. If delivery is recorded but warehouse receipt is not, provide the delivery event and the relevant order reference.

Warehouse and packing

Review unresolved inspection decisions, parcel selections, address details and any payment or service confirmation requested. A stored item is not necessarily a submitted parcel.

International movement

Use the parcel reference and latest carrier event. Check for information requests, collection instructions or a delivery exception before simply waiting for another scan.

These are investigation categories, not guaranteed causes. A quiet status might reflect a processing step, a delayed update or an actual problem. The useful response is to locate the missing evidence and the party handling that stage. Avoid repeatedly resubmitting an order or creating a duplicate parcel because the screen has not changed.

Handle tracking that is not updating

First, compare the current record with the service information supplied for your route. Use its stated processing expectations and contact instructions, including whether the number has merely been created or a handover has been confirmed. A generated label is different from evidence that a carrier physically accepted the package.

Next, check for a different reference at the handoff stage and for messages that need your response. Do not invent a universal number of days after which every LoloBuy parcel is considered lost. Different services, destinations and investigation procedures can have different conditions. The relevant conditions are those attached to your transaction.

If the status remains unclear, send one concise inquiry with the correct references and the last event. Keep the response with your timeline. When following up, add the new evidence or explain which point remains unanswered. Multiple messages with different numbers and no chronology can make the same issue harder to resolve.

Build a useful support record

  • Identify the product order or international parcel you are asking about.
  • Include the selected route and destination country where relevant.
  • Record the last event text, its timestamp and when you checked it.
  • Describe the mismatch: for example, domestic delivery shown but no corresponding warehouse record.
  • State the clarification you need, such as confirmation of physical handover or the next required action.
  • Attach only the relevant evidence through the official support channel available in your account.

Keep private order records private. A public discussion does not need your full address, telephone number, payment record, account identifier or complete tracking details. Redact those before sharing a screenshot. Preserve the unredacted original securely for the service provider if it is needed for an investigation.

A timeline example that avoids the wrong conclusion

Imagine three items from two sellers. Seller A's package is marked delivered to the warehouse, while Seller B's order still shows a dispatch stage. You have not yet submitted an international parcel. Searching the domestic number and seeing “delivered” does not mean the haul was delivered to your home; it refers to the seller-to-warehouse leg.

Record Seller A's item receipt and any inspection task separately from Seller B's outstanding order. Decide whether waiting for the second seller remains useful under your current storage and parcel plan. Only after accepted items are selected and the parcel process is arranged should you expect an international reference for that shipment.

This hypothetical example illustrates why the noun matters: item, domestic package or international parcel. It does not describe an actual customer's order or promise a particular sequence of screen labels. You can apply the same method to your own timeline without guessing where the parcel must be.

Respond to delivery exceptions with evidence

When tracking shows a delivery attempt, collection instruction or an information request, read the event carefully and check the recipient details. Follow the current instructions of the service handling the shipment. Do not assume that redelivery, address changes or return transport are automatically included.

If an event claims delivery and you cannot locate the parcel, preserve the event and any delivery evidence available. Check the delivery location or authorised recipient arrangements, then contact the relevant support channel with a clear description. Avoid making a loss claim based only on a shorthand label when the underlying event has not been examined.

For visible damage, keep the packaging and document what arrived. The availability and scope of an investigation or claim depend on the purchased service and its terms. The article provides an evidence method, not a guarantee of reimbursement or a legal interpretation of a delivery dispute.

Connect tracking with your parcel plan

Good tracking begins before dispatch. Use the domestic shipping guide to organise seller packages, the QC guide to close inspection decisions, and the shipping page to record the final route and parcel details. A single clear timeline reduces confusion when the next event is delayed.

domestic shipping guide · QC guide · shipping page

Scope checked 4 October 2026. LoloBuy's official app listing describes international shipping, but does not establish universal tracking labels or delivery times. This guide uses independent record-keeping and troubleshooting methods; verify all account actions, route conditions and support instructions against the current service.

/articles/shipping-cost-preparation.title: LoloBuy Shipping Cost Preparation
/articles/shipping-cost-preparation.description: Prepare a LoloBuy parcel by checking actual weight, volumetric size, route eligibility, consolidation and the final live shipping quote.
/articles/shipping-cost-preparation.body:
International shipping is not a fixed percentage of the product price. The useful estimate begins with the actual parcel: destination, weight, dimensions, item types, packaging and the routes currently available at checkout.

Separate product cost from parcel cost

Keep product price, domestic delivery, optional services, payment conversion and international shipping in separate spreadsheet columns. This prevents a low product price from being mistaken for a low delivered cost. Any USD value shown on a discovery page is an estimate; the live checkout determines the payable amount.

Use actual weight when available

Seller estimates can help with early planning, but warehouse and packed-parcel data are more relevant. Shoes, jackets, accessories with hardware and electronics can add weight quickly. Record each warehouse weight and compare it with the final parcel weight after packaging decisions.

Understand volumetric weight

Some routes use dimensions as well as scale weight. Large boxes, bulky clothing and protective packaging can increase billable volume even when the parcel is not especially heavy. Consolidation is not automatically cheaper if combining items produces a much larger package.

Group compatible items

Plan groups by protection and route compatibility. Soft clothing, rigid shoe boxes, fragile goods, batteries, liquids and other restricted categories may need different handling or routes. One sensitive item can narrow the available choices for the whole parcel, so compare separate and combined options using the live interface.

Compare current route conditions

Check route eligibility for the destination and item types, tracking level, estimated delivery window, declared-content requirements and visible restrictions. Another buyer’s quote may not apply to your destination, parcel or date. Rates and route availability can change, so use current checkout information.

Review optional packaging

Protective options can be valuable for fragile or shape-sensitive goods, but they may add weight or volume. Decide based on the product and current warehouse choices rather than applying every option automatically. If retail packaging is not essential, compare the protection tradeoff before requesting removal.

Before parcel submission

  • All items have an accepted QC status.
  • Destination and recipient details are correct.
  • Actual weight and parcel dimensions are reviewed.
  • Item types meet the selected route conditions.
  • Packaging choices are intentional.
  • Coupon or route discount is visibly applied, if eligible.
  • The final live quote and current terms are checked before payment.

A good shipping estimate is a range until the packed parcel and route are known. Keep the final result in your records so future estimates are based on comparable parcels rather than an unrelated advertised rate.

Independent guide: Always verify the live product, order, warehouse and parcel pages before paying because availability, services, routes and fees can change.

← View all articles

Compare the same parcel under two scenarios

Write down one baseline before experimenting: selected items, actual weight, outside dimensions, route, packaging and quote time. Then change one choice, such as retaining or removing suitable retail packaging. Record the new dimensions and quote where available. A comparison made with different items or destinations cannot isolate the effect of that packing choice.

Use the consolidation model to compare complete parcels. A larger combined box may reduce repeated base charges while increasing billable volume. Neither consolidation nor splitting is automatically the cheaper outcome.

consolidation model

Keep estimates and payments in separate columns

A hypothetical $70 estimate followed by an $82 final quote is a $12 difference. That calculation alone does not explain why it changed. Compare the packed dimensions, chargeable weight, route, selected services and discounts. Record any difference that remains unexplained and ask for clarification before treating it as a routine fee.

Do not copy another customer's per-kilogram figure into your own budget without checking the relevant route and parcel. A base charge, rounding rule or excluded service may make the apparent rate misleading. The estimate-versus-final guide provides a more complete comparison.

estimate-versus-final guide

Prepare for the tracking stage

Once the parcel is arranged, save its reference separately from the domestic seller numbers. Use the tracking guide to record the last confirmed event and next action. Keep the final quote and packing record with that parcel so that later questions can be tied to the correct shipment.

tracking guide

/guides/lolobuy-actual-vs-volumetric-wei.title: LoloBuy Actual vs Volumetric Weight: Which One Controls Shipping Cost?
/guides/lolobuy-actual-vs-volumetric-wei.description: Compare LoloBuy actual weight and volumetric weight, identify the route's billing rule, and test packaging changes before paying for a parcel.
/guides/lolobuy-actual-vs-volumetric-wei.body:
Independent billable-weight guide

A parcel can be light on a scale and still occupy expensive cargo space. That is why a useful LoloBuy cost record needs two separate numbers: actual weight and volumetric weight. The number that matters for payment depends on the live route's billing rule, so the goal is not to memorize one formula. It is to capture the final parcel evidence, read the selected route correctly and test only the packaging changes that could alter the chargeable result.

Current platform boundary: LoloBuy's public shipping interface can describe a line as charging by actual weight, by volumetric weight, or by the greater of the two. Where a volume formula applies, the displayed divisor belongs to that route. Confirm it in the current result instead of treating an old divisor as universal.

Start with three different weight fields

Actual weight is the parcel's measured mass on a scale. It should refer to the packed parcel, not merely the sum of seller estimates. The carton, tape, padding, corner protection and other packing materials add mass. If your worksheet uses the weights of individual warehouse items, label that total as provisional until the final parcel is weighed.

Volumetric weight converts external parcel volume into a weight-like number using a route formula. It represents the space a package occupies rather than its mass. Length, width and height therefore need to describe the outside of the closed carton. Product dimensions, shoe-box dimensions or a loose stack of clothing are not substitutes for the outbound package.

Chargeable weight is the billing result after the route applies its rule. It can equal actual weight, volumetric weight or the greater value. A planner should never rename an early estimate “chargeable weight” before choosing a route. LoloBuy's current parcel wording also distinguishes estimated chargeable weight from final chargeable weight after weigh-in, which is a useful reminder that the stage matters.

Read the route rule before doing arithmetic

The same parcel can produce different billable results on different lines. One line may state that it uses actual weight. Another may state that it uses volumetric weight. A third may compare the two and select the larger value. Record that sentence or billing label exactly as displayed beside the current route.

If the interface provides a divisor, save it with the route name, destination and calculation date. Do not keep a naked divisor in a permanent spreadsheet cell. A copied number loses the evidence needed to know where it came from, and it may remain in the sheet after the route changes or disappears.

Live billing descriptionNumber to useWhat could change the resultCommon mistake
Calculated by actual weightFinal packed scale weight, subject to the line's billing incrementRemoving or adding physical packing massReducing carton size while ignoring added padding weight
Calculated by volumetric weightVolume calculation using the divisor shown for that lineExternal length, width or heightUsing product dimensions instead of carton dimensions
Greater of actual and volumetric weightThe higher of the two calculated valuesEither mass or external dimensionsOptimizing the smaller value, which does not control billing

Build an auditable parcel-weight worksheet

One row should represent one parcel scenario on one route. Include the destination, included item IDs, packing assumption, actual weight, three external dimensions, route name, route billing description, displayed divisor when applicable, volumetric result, chargeable result, estimate date and confidence level. Preserve the original units rather than converting back and forth through several sheets.

Give each measurement a source. “Warehouse item total” is weaker than “final parcel weigh-in.” “Seller box dimensions” are weaker than “closed outbound carton.” A low-confidence row is still useful for planning when its uncertainty is visible. It becomes dangerous only when guesses are formatted to look final.

  1. List the exact items in the parcel and confirm their QC decisions are closed.
  2. Record the strongest available scale weight and mark whether packing is complete.
  3. Record external length, width and height in the unit requested by the live tool.
  4. Select the real destination and truthful product properties.
  5. Copy the current line's billing rule and divisor, if a divisor is shown.
  6. Calculate both weights, then apply the route rule to identify the controlling number.
  7. Save the dated estimate without overwriting the assumptions.
  8. Replace provisional inputs with final parcel data and reconcile the difference.

Worked example: find the controlling variable

Suppose a hypothetical packed parcel weighs 3.2 kg and measures 44 × 32 × 28 cm. These figures are an editorial example, not a LoloBuy quote. First, open the current result for the real destination and record the selected line's billing statement. If that line shows a volume formula using a divisor represented here as D, calculate:

Volumetric weight = length × width × height ÷ D
Use one consistent unit system and the exact formula displayed for the selected line. Do not insert a remembered value for D.

If the live line says it charges by actual weight, 3.2 kg is the relevant starting value even if the volume calculation is higher. If it says it charges by volumetric weight, the calculated volume figure controls. If it says it uses the greater value, compare the two before evaluating any packing change.

Now test one controlled alternative: 42 × 30 × 24 cm with the same 3.2 kg scale weight. This scenario asks whether a smaller carton could change the controlling volume result. It does not claim that warehouse staff can or should produce those dimensions. If the smaller result remains above actual weight, dimension reduction may still matter. If it drops below actual weight on a greater-of-two route, further size reduction will not lower the controlling weight unless mass also changes or the line has another billing increment.

Use a break-even test before changing packaging

The practical question is not “Can the carton be smaller?” but “Would a realistic change cross a billing threshold without creating a worse protection or eligibility problem?” Begin by identifying whether actual or volumetric weight controls the current scenario. If actual weight is already higher on a greater-of-two route, removing empty space alone may produce no shipping benefit.

Next, identify which dimension creates avoidable space. A long rigid item may set the carton length even when the rest is soft. A retail box may control height. Combining mismatched shapes can create voids that require filler. Record the cause rather than requesting “minimum volume” with no protection criteria.

Finally, compare the live estimated amount for the original and alternative scenario while keeping destination, item properties and route constant. A packaging decision is justified only when the possible saving outweighs the value of the box or protection being removed. Do not assign an invented damage probability. State the observable trade-off: less external volume versus less structure, different item arrangement or added handling.

Recognize measurements that should not be combined

Do not multiply dimensions from different sources. A seller's length, a warehouse photo's width and your guessed height do not describe one real box. Do not add the volumes of separate products and call the sum a consolidated carton; packing geometry and void space make that inference unreliable.

Do not compare a pre-packing actual weight with post-packing dimensions as though they were captured at the same stage. Keep a timestamp or stage label beside each record. If final weight is available but final dimensions are not, the greater-of-two result remains unresolved.

Rounding also matters. Store the raw measurement shown by the current record, then let the live route apply its own increments and calculation rules. Rounding every item upward before consolidation or rounding the final chargeable value yourself can create a number that does not match checkout.

Diagnose a final chargeable-weight change

Place the estimate and final record side by side. Compare included items, packing state, actual weight, each external dimension, route, divisor, billing type and any visible weight increment. Change explanations should point to evidence. “Height increased from the draft measurement after reinforcement” is traceable. “The calculator was wrong” is not enough when the inputs were different.

If the final number is unexpectedly high, verify unit entry first. Then check whether the longest sides were assigned correctly, whether the final carton includes an extra outer box and whether a different route formula was selected. If the source remains unclear, keep the difference marked as unresolved and use the current support channel with the saved parcel and route records.

The earlier shipping-calculator guide explains how to audit all estimator inputs. This guide has a narrower job: identify which weight controls one line. Keep currency effects in the exchange-rate worksheet so a conversion difference is not confused with a weight difference.

shipping-calculator guide · exchange-rate worksheet

Continue the parcel-cost workflow

Use the total landed-cost worksheet for the complete budget, keep domestic seller freight separate, and review the shipping overview before submitting the final parcel.

total landed-cost worksheet · domestic seller freight · shipping overview

/guides/lolobuy-consolidate-or-split-par.title: LoloBuy Consolidate or Split Parcels: A Complete Cost Model
/guides/lolobuy-consolidate-or-split-par.description: Compare one consolidated LoloBuy parcel with two split parcels using live eligibility, billable weight, packing, fees, deadlines and risk costs.
/guides/lolobuy-consolidate-or-split-par.body:
Independent parcel-grouping cost guide

Combining everything into one carton can remove duplicated parcel charges, but it can also create a larger billable weight, narrow the available routes or concentrate every item in one shipment. Splitting can solve a compatibility problem while repeating other costs. This guide shows LoloBuy shipping and cost planners how to compare one consolidated parcel with two complete split-parcel scenarios using the same warehouse items, current route evidence and explicit assumptions.

Current platform boundary: LoloBuy's current public interface says users can choose a product combination and submit a package, after which items are packed, weighed and shipped. Its rehearsal flow also accepts selected warehouse items for pre-packing and freight estimation. These facts support scenario planning, but they do not prove that one grouping is cheapest. This article publishes no fixed route, fee, weight divisor, transit time or universal parcel limit.

Start with compatibility, not a shipping-price guess

The first question is whether the same route can carry every intended item to the destination. Record each warehouse item's current property or restriction label, then run the complete item set through the live route screen. If one item removes an otherwise suitable option, note exactly which property caused the conflict. Do not assume that “ordinary-looking” products share the same eligibility.

A consolidated scenario is valid only when the whole group is accepted under one current route and one truthful declaration plan. A split scenario needs the same test for each proposed parcel. Splitting a sensitive item away from ordinary goods may restore a route for the ordinary group, but that does not mean the sensitive parcel automatically has a route of its own.

Compatibility also includes physical packing. A rigid box, compressible garment and fragile accessory may technically travel together while creating empty space or protection conflicts. Write the reason for grouping them: shared route, efficient nesting, a common deadline or simply avoiding a second parcel. If the reason cannot be stated, the proposed carton is not ready for a cost comparison.

Freeze one item set and create three scenario rows

Use the same item IDs and quantities in every scenario. Row A is one consolidated parcel. Rows B1 and B2 are the two parts of the split. The split total is B1 plus B2; neither row can be omitted because it looks inconvenient. Save the destination, capture time, currency and packing state beside all three rows.

Choose the split rule before requesting estimates. You might separate restricted from ordinary items, bulky from compact items, fragile from compressible items, or urgent from non-urgent items. A vague “half and half” split makes later analysis difficult. Record which item moves and why, then keep that assignment fixed while comparing costs.

Comparison rule: do not compare a rehearsed consolidated carton with two guessed product-weight totals and call the difference a saving. Use evidence of similar strength. If only the one-parcel version has warehouse packing data, label the split result provisional until equivalent inputs exist.

Build a complete cost stack for every parcel

  1. Current international freight. Save the live amount, currency, route, capture time and whether it is an estimate or final charge.
  2. Billable weight evidence. Record packed actual weight, external dimensions, displayed volumetric result and the route's current billing basis.
  3. Parcel-level charges. Copy every displayed handling, service or payment amount that repeats when a second parcel is created.
  4. Packing choices. Record only services actually selected for that parcel, plus their visible price and effect on weight or size when known.
  5. Insurance or protection cost. Include it only when offered for the exact parcel and route; preserve the live coverage terms separately.
  6. Destination-side reserve. Budget customs, tax or local handling from current official destination rules without assuming consolidation changes legal liability.
  7. Contingency. Add a clearly labelled reserve for remaining uncertainty rather than hiding it inside the freight line.

Never count seller-to-warehouse delivery again at the parcel stage unless a new charge actually appears. Those domestic costs were created by the purchase orders, not by choosing one outbound carton or two. Likewise, a product price does not change merely because its warehouse item is assigned to another parcel.
