Included item IDsComplete frozen setNamed subsetRemaining named subset
Eligible current routeRoute A or noneRoute BRoute C
Packed actual weightMeasured or labelled estimateMeasured or labelled estimateMeasured or labelled estimate
External dimensionsL × W × H for carton AL × W × H for carton BL × W × H for carton C
Billable weightCurrent route resultCurrent route resultCurrent route result
Freight plus parcel costsA freight + A extrasB freight + B extrasC freight + C extras
Total comparedA complete totalB complete total + C complete total

The arithmetic is simple only after the inputs are comparable. Consolidated total equals its current freight plus its parcel-level charges, selected packing costs, protection cost, destination reserve and contingency. Split total equals that same stack for parcel 1 plus the complete stack for parcel 2. The lower number wins only after both choices pass eligibility and protection checks.

Consider a fictional example in generic units. The one-parcel scenario has freight 84, parcel costs 6 and contingency 12, for 102. Two split scenarios total 49 plus 4 plus 7, and 38 plus 4 plus 6, for 108. Consolidation is six units lower in this example. These are teaching values, not LoloBuy prices. If the larger carton loses its intended route or needs extra protection, the result must be recalculated with the new live evidence.

Test the geometry instead of adding product dimensions

Individual product measurements do not reveal the final consolidated carton. Items can nest, compress, stack or force void space; retail boxes and protective material alter every side. Record the packing stage for each measurement. Seller dimensions, warehouse item dimensions, rehearsal dimensions and final outbound dimensions are different evidence objects.

A larger carton can have a higher volumetric result even when its scale weight barely changes. Two smaller cartons repeat packaging mass but may use space more efficiently. Which effect controls depends on the current route's billing rule and increments. Copy that rule from each live result rather than importing a remembered divisor.

Change one thing at a time. First compare the complete one-versus-two grouping with the same protection level. Then test a packing alternative inside the preferred grouping. If you remove boxes, change reinforcement and split the item set simultaneously, the final difference cannot be attributed to any single decision.

Add timing and risk without inventing probabilities

One-parcel concentration

One shipment creates one tracking chain and one delivery event, but every item shares the same delay, damage or loss event. Record the value and urgency concentrated in the carton; do not assign an unsupported probability.

Two-parcel exposure

Two shipments create two tracking chains, possible arrival on different days and two evidence records. They can separate urgent or fragile items, but they also repeat tasks and may require separate claim documentation.

Deadlines can change the answer. Waiting for a late seller item may delay the entire consolidated group. A split can release warehouse-ready items while the remaining item continues through QC, but only if current storage, return and personal delivery deadlines support that choice. Write the latest acceptable submission date for each group.

Use a risk adjustment only when it reflects your decision, not a fabricated platform statistic. For example, you may value arriving before a personal deadline at ten generic units or cap the merchandise value you are willing to place in one carton. Label such numbers as personal planning values. They are not expected losses, carrier performance scores or insurance guarantees.

Know the common comparison failures

Comparing route names instead of payable totals: the same label can be irrelevant if the parcels have different billable weights or eligibility. Ignoring the second parcel: every repeated charge and packing choice belongs in the split total. Using mixed dates: route availability and prices captured on different days do not form a clean experiment.

Overwriting old evidence: keep the early estimate, rehearsal result, submitted parcel and final charge as separate rows. A visible variance improves the next plan. Replacing every earlier value with the last one makes the worksheet look accurate while erasing how the decision was made.

Use a final submit-or-rebuild checklist

  • Every scenario contains the same complete warehouse item set with no duplicated or missing quantity.
  • The reason for the split is recorded and each proposed parcel passes current route screening.
  • Weight, dimensions and billable weight describe the same packing stage within each comparison.
  • One-parcel and two-parcel quotes were captured for the same destination, currency and decision window.
  • All repeated parcel charges, packing choices, protection costs and contingencies are included.
  • Fragile, bulky, compressible and route-sensitive items have compatible protection plans.
  • Warehouse, QC, return and personal delivery deadlines support the chosen grouping.
  • Personal risk values are labelled as assumptions, not platform or carrier statistics.
  • The final checkout is rechecked because an earlier estimate is not a locked price.
  • The saved decision record identifies why the winning scenario was chosen.

The best LoloBuy parcel grouping is not automatically the carton with the most items or the fewest labels. It is the lowest complete, currently eligible cost for a packing plan that meets protection and timing requirements. Compare one finished scenario with two finished scenarios, preserve the evidence behind each number, and rebuild the model whenever the item set, route or packing state changes.

/guides/lolobuy-currency-conversion-exch.title: LoloBuy Currency Conversion: Calculate the Real Exchange-Rate Cost
/guides/lolobuy-currency-conversion-exch.description: Calculate LoloBuy currency conversion from the amount sent, CNY credited and dated platform rate, then separate payment fees and bank-side costs.
/guides/lolobuy-currency-conversion-exch.body:
Independent cost-planning guide

The useful LoloBuy exchange-rate question is not “Is the rate good?” It is: “How much source currency left my payment method, how much CNY reached the account, which dated platform rate was shown, and which costs belong to the bank or payment channel?” Record those four facts before comparing a quote with another option.

Current official rule checked: LoloBuy’s payment-method page says bank-transfer funds are converted at the LoloBuy website exchange rate and credits CNY as the remittance amount received multiplied by that platform rate. The page does not publish one permanent rate. The live value and credited amount must therefore be captured for each transaction.

Define the three rates before calculating a difference

A currency comparison can contain three different rates. The platform rate is the rate LoloBuy displays or applies when converting the amount it receives into CNY. The provider rate is the conversion used by your bank, card network or local payment method when it debits your account. A public reference rate is a dated market indicator used for context. These values do not have to match, and a difference does not identify its cause by itself.

Keep the direction explicit. “CNY per USD” is not interchangeable with “USD per CNY.” LoloBuy’s current bank-transfer formula is expressed as received remittance multiplied by the website exchange rate to obtain credited CNY, so the rate in that equation is CNY per unit of remittance currency. If a screen uses the inverse direction, invert it before comparing: one divided by the quoted rate.

Do not call the whole difference a hidden fee. It may contain platform conversion, payment processing, bank charges, cross-border fees, rounding and timing. The correct first label is observed conversion difference for this dated transaction. Assign a narrower cause only when the current screen or provider record names it.

Build a same-moment currency worksheet

Save one row before confirmation and one row after crediting. The first row should contain date and time, selected account currency, payment method, amount you intend to send, named fee, final platform amount and displayed exchange rate. The second should contain the amount actually debited, debit currency, provider fee if itemized, amount received by LoloBuy, CNY credited and credit time.

FieldBefore paymentAfter credit
Source amountAmount enteredAmount actually debited
Named chargePlatform or channel line shownProvider fee shown separately
RateDated platform quote and directionObserved rate from credited CNY
Destination valueExpected CNY creditActual CNY account credit
EvidenceNon-sensitive payment summaryCredit record and redacted statement

Redact names, card digits, bank references, addresses and account identifiers before using a screenshot in a shared record. A useful audit needs amounts, currencies, labels and timestamps—not private financial details. If LoloBuy receives less than you sent because an intermediary deducted a charge, use the amount received in the platform formula and keep the deduction in a separate field.

Calculate the observed rate and effective cost

Observed credit rate

Divide CNY credited by the remittance amount LoloBuy says it received. Suppose an illustrative transfer delivers 100 source-currency units to the platform and the account receives 710 CNY. The observed credit rate is 710 ÷ 100 = 7.10 CNY per source unit. Those numbers are teaching values, not a current LoloBuy rate.

End-to-end rate

For the buyer’s complete result, divide CNY credited by the amount actually debited in the same source currency. If the provider debits 103 units while 710 CNY reaches the account, the end-to-end rate is 710 ÷ 103, or about 6.893 CNY per unit. This captures the combined effect, but it still does not prove which party caused every difference.

Reference difference

Take a public reference rate from nearly the same time and in the same direction. If the illustrative reference were 7.20 CNY per unit, the expected reference value for 103 units would be 741.6 CNY. The difference from the observed 710 CNY is 31.6 CNY, or about 4.26% of that reference value. Report it as a dated end-to-end difference, not as a permanent platform markup.

Reusable formulas:
Observed platform rate = CNY credited ÷ remittance received.
End-to-end rate = CNY credited ÷ source currency actually debited.
Reference difference % = (reference CNY value − credited CNY) ÷ reference CNY value × 100.

Keep payment-method fees separate from exchange rate

A named fee and an exchange-rate difference answer different questions. If a 5% processing line is shown, record it as processing. Then calculate conversion from the amount reaching the account and the CNY credited. Do not hide the processing line inside an implied rate and later count it again as a separate fee. The service and payment fee guide covers that broader checkout audit.

service and payment fee guide

Compare methods with one fixed CNY target

Choose the CNY balance you actually need, then work backward. A product order and a later parcel payment may require different balances; do not top up a large round amount merely because one method advertises a lower fee. For each available method, record how much source currency is needed to reach the same CNY target after named fees and conversion.

Hold time as constant as practical. Compare live nonbinding quotes within a short window, without confirming payments merely to collect data. Use the same source currency, CNY target and account. A method is not cheaper because its separate fee line is lower if the final source-currency debit is higher. The decision column should therefore rank the final amount debited for the target CNY, expected credit timing and any provider-side charge you can support.

Availability can depend on country, account and current interface. The official page lists several international and local options, but that does not prove every method will appear for every user. Report what the current account displays. Do not borrow another buyer’s payment option or currency result and present it as universally available.

Handle refunds and unused balance without inventing a rate

A later refund can return to platform balance, a payment channel or another destination depending on the current transaction terms. Its currency and conversion may not mirror the original funding. Save the original source amount, CNY credit, purchase debit, refund amount, destination and dates as separate events. Do not assume a refund reverses the original exchange rate exactly.

Unused account balance also has an opportunity cost. It is CNY already converted at a historical transaction result. When comparing a future order, distinguish existing balance from new funding; otherwise the old rate can make a new payment method look artificially cheap or expensive. This guide does not claim a withdrawal rule, refund time or deduction because those outcomes require the current account and policy evidence.

Final LoloBuy exchange-rate audit

  1. Record the source and CNY currencies in the correct direction.
  2. Capture the platform rate and timestamp before payment.
  3. Separate every named payment or provider charge.
  4. Use the remittance amount received in LoloBuy’s credit formula.
  5. Verify the actual CNY credited instead of relying on an estimate.
  6. Calculate both platform-observed and end-to-end rates.
  7. Compare with a same-time public reference only as context.
  8. Label unexplained differences without guessing the responsible party.
  9. Keep refund and unused-balance events separate.
  10. Recheck current payment terms before the next top-up.

A useful LoloBuy currency record is transaction-specific. It tells a cost planner what left the payment account, what arrived at the platform, what CNY was credited and what each named charge covered. That evidence is more actionable than a headline exchange rate because it can be reconciled after payment and compared fairly the next time.

Evidence ledger and editorial limits

Official LoloBuy source checked 28 August 2026: the current “What kinds of payment methods are available on LoloBuy?” page. It supplied the bank-transfer conversion formula, dated fee statements and credit-time descriptions used above. The public homepage was also checked for the current English/USD display and multi-stage purchasing, warehouse and shipping context.

Technical comparison boundaries were cross-checked with the current Visa and Mastercard currency-conversion tools. The worksheet, illustrative numbers, formulas, fixed-CNY comparison and refund-ledger method are independent LoloBuyChina editorial analysis. No permanent LoloBuy rate, markup, top-up availability, refund result or future fee is asserted.

/guides/lolobuy-domestic-shipping-seller.title: LoloBuy Domestic Shipping: Track the Seller-to-Warehouse Stage
/guides/lolobuy-domestic-shipping-seller.description: Track LoloBuy domestic shipping from a Chinese seller to the warehouse, separate the cost from international freight, and diagnose status delays with evidence.
/guides/lolobuy-domestic-shipping-seller.body:
LoloBuy's public homepage showed 180 days of free storage on 31 October 2026. Confirm the deadline and eligibility for each item in your account. Storage time does not extend a seller's return window.

Independent shipping-stage guide

LoloBuy domestic shipping is the China-side movement from a marketplace seller to the purchasing warehouse. It happens after the product order is accepted and before warehouse QC, consolidation or international parcel submission. Track it as a separate cost and status chain: seller handling, courier dispatch, delivery scan and warehouse intake.

Know which shipping stage you are looking at

A reverse-shopping-agent order has at least two transport stages. First, the Chinese seller sends the item to the agent's warehouse. Later, accepted warehouse items are prepared for international delivery. Those stages involve different addresses, carriers, evidence and costs. A seller dispatch scan is not international dispatch, and a domestic tracking number is not necessarily the number that will follow the final parcel to your destination.

Keep four records separate: the seller's order or purchase status; the China domestic courier record; the warehouse receipt and QC record; and the later international parcel record. When a page says “shipped,” ask which actor shipped what to whom. That one question prevents most status confusion.

The stage is complete only when the correct item is associated with your warehouse account and ready for the relevant intake or QC review. A courier “delivered” event can be useful evidence, but it does not by itself prove that the warehouse has identified, processed and photographed the item.

Separate domestic freight from product and international cost

Record the product amount and seller-to-warehouse delivery as different fields. A listing may show free domestic delivery, a fixed amount, a destination-dependent charge or no usable figure until the order is created. Zero should mean the live order explicitly shows no charge; blank should mean you have not confirmed it. Do not copy the cheapest option's freight to another size, seller or listing.

When several items come from one seller, check whether the current order treats them as separate shipments or a combined seller dispatch. Do not assume one domestic charge will cover every item. A seller can split stock, dispatch from different locations or send an incomplete quantity. Preserve the order-level breakdown rather than dividing a shared amount into invented item prices.

The domestic cost belongs in a total landed-cost worksheet, but it should not be confused with international freight. The later parcel quote depends on accepted items, packed weight and dimensions, available routes and current terms. Paying China-side delivery does not establish the final shipping cost.

total landed-cost worksheet

FieldWhat to recordDo not assume
ProductExact variant, quantity, live order amountHeadline price equals selected price
Domestic freightDisplayed seller-to-warehouse amountIt is included or free
International freightLater packed quote and routeDomestic tracking predicts it
Destination reserveSeparate researched allowancePrevious parcel treatment repeats

Read the status chain as a sequence of responsibilities

Order submitted or purchasing

At this point the product link and selected option should be unambiguous. Save the source URL, seller name where visible, color, size, version, quantity and the amounts displayed. If purchasing is waiting on clarification, domestic shipping has not meaningfully begun. Resolve option questions before treating the seller as late.

Seller processing or awaiting dispatch

This normally means the purchasing stage exists but no useful carrier movement has been recorded. Stock confirmation, order handling or a seller question may still be open. The official public page does not provide one guaranteed seller dispatch time, so compare the current status, any seller note and the order's displayed dates instead of applying a borrowed deadline.

Domestic dispatched or in transit

Record the China courier name when shown, domestic tracking identifier, first acceptance scan and latest event. A number without a carrier acceptance event may be newly created, entered incorrectly or waiting for pickup. Translate the event, not just the status label, and keep the original text if the wording is uncertain.

Delivered to warehouse

Save the delivery date, time, city or facility clue and any recipient marker that appears in the domestic record. Then wait for the warehouse-side item to be matched and processed. A busy intake period can create a gap between courier delivery and account visibility. That gap is a warehouse handoff question, not an international-carrier delay.

Warehouse received and QC available

Confirm that the warehouse entry belongs to the correct order and quantity. LoloBuy publicly describes warehouse inspection and photographs, but the public page does not define a universal photo set or processing time. Review the evidence shown for the actual item. Domestic shipping is now historical evidence; the next decision is acceptance, a focused question or the current order action.

Diagnose a domestic-shipping delay from the last reliable event

Start with the last event, not the total number of days. If there is no seller dispatch, the seller or purchasing handoff is the open stage. If a tracking number exists without acceptance, the seller-to-courier handoff is unclear. If the parcel has moving courier scans, the domestic carrier owns the current transport stage. If it shows delivered but no warehouse item appears, focus on matching and intake.

Use elapsed time only in context. Compare the order's own dates, stated seller conditions and support options. Weekends, public events, stock arrangements and local courier exceptions can affect movement, but do not invent one of those explanations for a specific order without evidence. A quiet tracking page tells you that no new public event is visible; it does not prove loss, seller fraud or warehouse error.

  • No purchase confirmation: verify that the source and option are complete.
  • No dispatch: save the order status and any seller handling note.
  • Number, no carrier scan: preserve when the number first appeared.
  • In transit, no movement: record the exact last location and event.
  • Delivered, no intake: compare tracking, order identity and warehouse-receipt status.
  • Partial arrival: match quantity and each domestic number before escalating.

Build a support-ready domestic shipping evidence pack

A useful request is short because the supporting record is complete. Include the order reference, exact selected variant, seller name if visible, domestic carrier and number, latest event with date, and the specific missing handoff. Attach the full tracking view and order status when the interface permits. A cropped “delivered” word without the number or timeline is weaker evidence.

Write an observable request: “Domestic tracking shows delivery to the warehouse area on 13 August, but the order has no warehouse-received entry; please check whether this tracking number has been matched.” That is more actionable than “package missing.” Do not demand an outcome the evidence does not establish.

Remove full addresses, payment details, account credentials and unrelated parcel numbers before sharing. Preserve originals privately. If a seller sent several parcels, list each identifier and quantity on its own line. If the platform shows a support action or deadline for the current order, use that live route promptly; this guide does not promise a refund, replacement or claim result.

Close the China-side record when the warehouse takes over

After intake, compare product identity, color, size or version, quantity and visible condition with the saved order. Use the QC photo checklist for that decision. A completed domestic shipment proves that something reached the warehouse process; it does not prove that the item matches, works, fits, is authentic or can use every international route.

QC photo checklist

When several accepted items are ready, consolidation becomes a new decision. Compare compatibility, dimensions, protection and current route eligibility before assuming one parcel is cheapest. The domestic freight already paid remains an item-stage cost; it should not be merged into the international quote or forgotten when calculating landed cost.

Seller-to-warehouse checklist

  1. Save the original product link and exact selected option.
  2. Record the displayed product amount and China domestic freight separately.
  3. Identify who currently owns the handoff: buyer, seller, courier or warehouse.
  4. Save the first scan, latest event and any delivery event with dates.
  5. Match every tracking number to its order and quantity.
  6. Do not treat courier delivery as completed warehouse intake.
  7. Review identity and QC evidence once the item appears in the warehouse.
  8. Carry domestic freight into the landed-cost worksheet as its own layer.

The practical goal is not to predict a perfect timeline. It is to know where the item is supposed to be, what evidence supports the last handoff and which party can answer the next question. That turns “LoloBuy domestic shipping” from one vague status into a traceable seller-to-warehouse record.

Evidence ledger and editorial limits

The handoff model, cost fields, status interpretation, delay tree and evidence checklist are independent LoloBuyChina editorial analysis. No fixed fee, delivery time, route, photo count, return window, refund outcome or customer experience is asserted.

Continue cost and warehouse planning

Open the landed-cost worksheet, review all buyer guides, and use the international shipping preparation guide only after accepted items and packed evidence exist.

/guides/lolobuy-parcel-dimensions-billab.title: LoloBuy Parcel Dimensions: Measure the Box That Actually Gets Billed
/guides/lolobuy-parcel-dimensions-billab.description: Measure LoloBuy parcel dimensions at the correct packing stage, check route size limits and reconcile the final box with billable weight.
/guides/lolobuy-parcel-dimensions-billab.body:
Independent parcel-measurement guide

Parcel dimensions are useful only when they describe one real package at a named stage. A seller's product box, a warehouse draft and the final closed export carton can all have different measurements. This guide shows LoloBuy shipping and cost planners how to record the longest external points, screen live route limits and reconcile the final box with billable weight without disguising estimates as facts.

Current platform boundary: LoloBuy's public shipping interface distinguishes estimated shipping from the final charge after weigh-in. Its rehearsal result can show estimated actual weight, dimensions and volumetric weight, while route results can display weight limits, dimension limits and a billing standard. Those fields are live, route-specific evidence. This article does not publish a permanent divisor, size limit, price or delivery time.

Define the object before writing three numbers

A dimension record should answer four questions: what was measured, who or what supplied the measurement, when in the packing process it was captured, and whether the carton was closed. Without those fields, a neat length × width × height entry can be attached to the wrong object.

Product dimensions describe the item itself. Retail-package dimensions describe a seller box or bag. Draft parcel dimensions may describe an estimated arrangement before final packing. Final outbound dimensions describe the closed parcel that is weighed for international shipment. Only the last record can explain the final carton as shipped, although earlier records remain valuable for planning.

Do not add the lengths of individual products or sum their volumes and call the result a parcel. Items nest, compress, stack and create voids. Padding, reinforcement and the outer carton also change the geometry. Treat any pre-packing total as a scenario, not a warehouse measurement.

Use one repeatable external-measurement protocol

The correct target is the smallest rectangular box that could enclose the finished parcel. Measurements therefore run between the parcel's farthest external points, not between convenient carton seams. Include tape folds, bulges, corner protectors, handles or other protrusions when they extend the outside profile.

  1. Confirm the stage. Record whether the package is a seller carton, rehearsal result or final outbound parcel. Never merge fields from different stages.
  2. Close the parcel. Measure after normal closure and external protection are in place. An open flap or an uncompressed soft bag does not represent the shipped shape.
  3. Find the longest side. Label it length for your worksheet, then measure the maximum outside-to-outside distance without rounding it down.
  4. Measure the second-longest side. Record it as width. Rotate the parcel rather than assuming the printed carton label defines orientation.
  5. Measure the remaining maximum side. Record height across the tallest external point, including a stable bulge or added protection.
  6. Save units and source. Keep centimetres or the interface's requested unit attached to every value, plus the record or screen from which it came.
  7. Repeat any unstable measurement. If a soft parcel changes shape, note the normal closed condition rather than forcing a temporary squeeze that packing will not hold.

Precision rule: preserve the value shown by the current warehouse or rehearsal record. Do not round each side downward to make an estimate fit a route limit. Let the live platform apply its own calculation and billing increments.

Keep a three-stage dimension ledger

A good worksheet does not overwrite the draft when better evidence arrives. It retains each stage so the difference can be explained. This is especially important when a packing request changes the outer carton or when reinforcement increases one side.

RecordWhat belongs in itConfidencePermitted use
Planning draftItem list, provisional weight, assumed outer dimensions, intended packingLow until warehouse evidence existsCompare scenarios and set a budget range
Rehearsal resultIncluded items, displayed estimated actual weight, dimensions, volume result and dateHigher, but still label it as rehearsalScreen routes and refine the expected charge
Final parcelFinal included items, closed-carton dimensions, scale weight, selected route and final chargeable weightBest record for the shipped parcelReconcile the bill and improve the next estimate

For every row, also save destination, route name, visible dimension limit, weight limit, billing standard and capture date. A line that is unavailable for one parcel may be available for another because the destination, product properties or package size differs. A route name alone is not enough context.

Pass the route-size gate before comparing prices

Route eligibility comes before price ranking. Select the real destination and truthful product properties, then compare the parcel's longest external sides with the dimension rules shown for each current result. Some interfaces may express limits per side; others may include combined-size or other conditions. Copy the wording rather than converting it into a rule the page did not state.

Use a small safety margin in planning because provisional measurements can change after final packing. The margin is an editorial planning choice, not a LoloBuy allowance. Never claim that a parcel “fits” when an assumed dimension merely equals a displayed maximum. Wait for the final record and current eligibility result.

Keep a route candidate

The destination is correct, product properties are truthful, all displayed size and weight conditions are satisfied, and the billing standard is recorded with a date.

Remove a route candidate

Any side exceeds a live limit, eligibility is unclear, the item property is incompatible, or the comparison relies on an old screenshot rather than the current parcel.

Only after this gate should you compare costs. Otherwise, the apparent cheapest option may be one the final parcel cannot use.

Worked example: isolate the dimension change

Consider a fictional planning draft of 46 × 34 × 25 cm and a rehearsal result of 48 × 35 × 27 cm. These are editorial examples, not LoloBuy measurements or route limits. The useful observation is not simply that “volume increased.” Length rose by 2 cm, width by 1 cm and height by 2 cm after the package moved from an assumption to a warehouse result.

Create two rows rather than replacing the draft. Attach the same intended item list to both, then verify whether the actual included items and packing request remained unchanged. If they did, the larger rehearsal dimensions may reflect real packing geometry that the draft missed. If reinforcement or an additional retail box was added, record that as a candidate explanation.

Next, run the rehearsal measurements through the current route result. When the route provides a volumetric formula, use its displayed divisor, represented here only as D: length × width × height ÷ D. The previous actual-versus-volumetric-weight guide explains how the route's billing standard selects the controlling number. This page has a narrower role: making sure the three inputs describe the correct outer box.

actual-versus-volumetric-weight guide

Finally, compare the final parcel against rehearsal. If the final dimensions are 48 × 35 × 28 cm, isolate the one-centimetre height change and check the final packing state. Do not blame the calculator when the input object changed. If all recorded fields match but the displayed result remains unexplained, save both records and ask support about the specific parcel and route.

Decide whether a packing change is worth testing

A smaller carton can help only when the proposed arrangement is physically realistic, stays eligible and preserves an acceptable protection level. Start with the dimension that is driving the current problem. A rigid long item may set length; a retail box may set height; an awkward combination may create unused width.

Change one assumption at a time. A “remove retail box” scenario should retain the same items, destination and candidate route so the dimensional effect remains visible. A “split parcel” scenario is a different decision because it creates two packages, two eligibility checks and potentially different fixed costs. Do not compare both at once and attribute the whole difference to carton size.

Reject a change when the expected benefit depends on squeezing a soft parcel into a shape that will not remain closed, removing protection you value, or assuming a route formula that is not displayed. Accept it for further review when the cause of empty space is clear, the revised external dimensions are plausible and a current eligible route produces a meaningful difference.

Audit a surprising final billable weight

Place planning, rehearsal and final records side by side. Check the included item IDs first. Then compare packing instructions, scale weight, all three external dimensions, measurement units, selected route, route divisor if shown, billing standard and any visible increment. This order prevents a currency or route change from being misdiagnosed as a measurement error.

Look for small dimensional changes across every side. Because volume multiplies length, width and height, modest increases can compound. Also check whether one measurement describes a product box while another describes the outer shipping carton. Those are not contradictory records; they are different objects.

If the final charge differs from an early estimate, preserve both values. The current interface itself distinguishes estimated and final shipping after weigh-in. A dated variance is useful evidence for the next parcel. Deleting the estimate removes the opportunity to learn which assumption was weak.

Final parcel-dimension checklist

  • The record names the exact parcel stage and included items.
  • Length, width and height describe the closed outer package.
  • Bulges, protection and protrusions are included at their longest points.
  • Units, source, capture date and confidence are saved with the values.
  • The real destination and truthful product properties are selected.
  • Every candidate route passes its current weight and dimension conditions.
  • The live billing standard and displayed divisor, if any, are preserved.
  • Draft, rehearsal and final values remain separate.
  • Any packing alternative changes one clear assumption and states the protection trade-off.
  • The final charge is reconciled with final evidence, not a seller estimate.

A reliable LoloBuy parcel-dimensions worksheet is not a collection of three numbers. It is a versioned record of one physical box, the route rules applied to it and the stage at which each value became known. That record makes size limits easier to screen, billable-weight changes easier to explain and future budgets less dependent on guesswork.

Continue the cost-planning workflow

Use the shipping-calculator audit to validate every estimator input, keep all parcel costs in the total landed-cost worksheet, and review the shipping overview before submitting the final package.

/guides/lolobuy-qc-photo-checklist-2026.title: LoloBuy QC Photos Guide 2026: Product Inspection Before International Shipping
/guides/lolobuy-qc-photo-checklist-2026.description: A detailed independent LoloBuy QC photos guide explaining product inspection, W2C research, warehouse checks and shipping preparation.
/guides/lolobuy-qc-photo-checklist-2026.body:
Independent buyer guide. Always verify current platform rules, seller information, product availability, inspection options and shipping quotes before payment.

Why QC Photos Matter

QC photos are a practical checkpoint between product purchase and international shipment. A buyer may find a product through a W2C link, spreadsheet card or marketplace page, but the warehouse photo is often the first chance to inspect the actual item that arrived. The photo cannot solve every risk, yet it helps identify obvious color differences, damaged packaging, wrong sizes, missing accessories and visible construction issues.

A good QC review is slow and specific. Instead of only asking whether the product “looks good,” buyers should compare the visible details with the original product page. Check the front, back, side view, labels, print position, materials and packaging. If the item is expensive, fragile or difficult to replace, a more careful inspection is worth the extra time.

How to Review Shoes

For shoes, start with overall symmetry. Compare the left and right shoe, toe box shape, heel height, sole balance, side panels and logo placement. Look for obvious glue marks, bent shapes, color mismatch or uneven stitching. If the product includes a box, extra laces, tags or dust bag, confirm whether they are visible in the warehouse photos.

Do not judge shoes only from one top-down image. A side view and heel view often reveal issues that are hidden from the front. If important areas are missing, check whether the order page allows additional detail photos.

How to Review Clothing

For clothing, measurements matter as much as appearance. Check the size tag, collar, sleeve shape, stitching, print scale, embroidery, fabric texture and labels. Large graphics should be reviewed for placement and alignment. Jackets and hoodies may need extra attention around zippers, drawstrings, cuffs and inner labels.

Color differences can happen because of lighting, screens and camera settings, so buyers should focus on whether the color appears obviously inconsistent with the product page. If sizing is critical, ask for measurement photos when available.

Accessories and Small Items

Bags, belts, jewelry and small accessories require close detail checks. Look at corners, metal parts, straps, zippers, stitching and included packaging. Small missing accessories can be easy to overlook, so compare the QC photos with the product description before approving shipment.

QC and Shipping Decisions

QC review should happen before shipping decisions. Once the product is approved, the buyer can consider parcel weight, package volume, shipping route and whether to keep or remove packaging. Heavy boxes and bulky packaging can affect the final quote, while fragile items may need better protection.

A Better QC Workflow

A simple workflow is: save the W2C route, purchase the item, wait for warehouse arrival, review QC photos, request extra checks if needed, then decide whether to ship. Keep notes in a spreadsheet so future purchases become easier to compare. This turns QC from a quick glance into a repeatable inspection system.

Keep a decision record for every item

Record the source item ID, ordered variant, warehouse reference, inspection date and decision. Use three states: accepted, needs clarification, or return requested. Describe the missing evidence rather than writing only “bad QC.” A replacement item needs a new inspection; an earlier approval does not apply automatically.

Request a measurement that answers your question

For clothing, name the measurement and the method: for example, flat chest width from armpit to armpit. For shoes, distinguish foot length from insole length. Save the seller's chart and its unit. A visible size label does not prove a universal US, UK or EU fit.

Know what a photograph cannot establish

A photo can show visible features and measurements, but cannot prove authenticity, durability, chemical composition or hidden performance. Lighting can change colour appearance. Treat another buyer's photos as reference material; inspect the actual warehouse item assigned to your order before shipment.

For an unresolved item, read the returns and refunds guide before submitting it in an international parcel.

/guides/lolobuy-rehearsal-shipping-cost-.title: LoloBuy Rehearsal Shipping: Measure Cost Before the Real Parcel
/guides/lolobuy-rehearsal-shipping-cost-.description: Use LoloBuy rehearsal shipping to refine parcel weight, dimensions and route estimates, then compare the live fee with the planning value it creates.
/guides/lolobuy-rehearsal-shipping-cost-.body:
Independent pre-packing cost guide

Rehearsal shipping is useful when better parcel evidence could change a route, packing or budget decision. It is not the international shipment itself, and its result is not the final bill. This guide helps LoloBuy shipping and cost planners capture the draft assumptions, live rehearsal fee, pre-packed weight and dimensions, revised route estimates and final outbound variance as one auditable record.

Current platform boundary: LoloBuy's live interface describes rehearsal as a simulation service for pre-packing and freight estimation, without creating a real shipment. After completion, the result can show estimated actual weight and dimensions; the platform warns that packaging materials, item condition and value-added services can make actual outbound data fluctuate. This article therefore publishes no fixed rehearsal fee, completion time, saving percentage or guaranteed final measurement.

Decide what uncertainty you are paying to reduce

Do not purchase rehearsal simply because a button exists. Write the unresolved decision first. Perhaps two live routes have different size thresholds, a bulky retail box may control chargeable weight, reinforcement could change the carton, or the early shipping range is too wide for the remaining budget. Rehearsal has planning value only when the result can alter a real choice.

Separate unknown parcel geometry from known preferences. Rehearsal may improve the weight and dimension evidence for a selected group of warehouse items. It cannot decide how much protection you personally need, guarantee destination customs treatment, make a restricted item eligible or predict a carrier delay. If the unresolved question lives outside packing and freight estimation, buying more parcel measurements may not answer it.

Write a decision sentence: “If pre-packed height is below the current threshold, keep route A; otherwise compare route B with a split.” The sentence names the measurable result and the action it controls. “I want a more accurate price” is too vague to audit later.

Freeze the draft before requesting a simulation

A rehearsal result can be interpreted only if the input set is preserved. Save every included warehouse item ID, quantity, declared product property and selected packing instruction. Record the destination and the date on which you viewed the route candidates. If one item arrives later or a service is added after rehearsal, the final parcel is no longer the same comparison object.

Capture the provisional actual weight, assumed dimensions, estimated chargeable weight and visible shipping range before paying. Label every field “draft.” The point is not to defend the early estimate; it is to discover which assumption changes. Deleting the draft after receiving better data removes the evidence needed to improve the next parcel plan.

Copy the rehearsal fee shown in the live checkout and its currency at the moment of purchase. The public interface exposes a rehearsal-fee field, but a current amount may depend on the account, parcel or service state. A number copied from an older guide is not evidence for the present request.

Use a seven-field rehearsal request record

  1. Item set. Save exact warehouse item identifiers, quantities and any excluded product.
  2. Destination. Record country or region because available routes and estimates depend on it.
  3. Packing instruction. Preserve only options actually selected, without assuming an unconfirmed service.
  4. Decision question. State the threshold, route or budget choice the result could change.
  5. Draft evidence. Keep provisional weight, dimensions, estimate, eligible routes and capture time.
  6. Live fee. Record the displayed rehearsal charge, currency and payment evidence without sharing private payment data.
  7. Result identity. Link the completed rehearsal record to the same item set and instruction version.

Version rule: if you add or remove an item, change protection or alter another packing instruction, create a new scenario row. Do not silently attach the old rehearsal result to a materially different final parcel.

Read the result as stronger evidence, not final truth

The completed rehearsal can provide an estimated actual weight and three dimensions. Save the values exactly as displayed, including units and completion time. If the result also shows volume or volumetric weight, copy the label used by the interface. Do not reverse-engineer a permanent divisor from one record and apply it to every route.

“Estimated” remains important. The platform's own warning says actual outbound data can fluctuate because of packaging materials, item condition, value-added services and similar factors. Treat rehearsal as a better pre-shipment observation, not a contractual final weigh-in. Keep a contingency reserve appropriate to the remaining uncertainty.

Re-run the current route comparison with the rehearsal measurements. Verify destination, product properties, weight limits, dimension limits and billing standard before looking at price. An apparently inexpensive route is irrelevant if the pre-packed parcel is not eligible. Save the new result beside the old one, with the same currency and date.

Calculate the information gained

FieldBefore rehearsalAfter rehearsalWhat changed
Included itemsDraft item IDs and quantitiesConfirmed simulation setAny difference invalidates a direct comparison
Actual weightProvisional warehouse totalDisplayed estimated pre-packed weightShows packaging and grouping effect
DimensionsAssumed or incompleteDisplayed pre-packed L × W × HImproves route and volume screening
Route setEarly candidatesCandidates eligible for current resultReveals whether a planned route survives
Shipping estimateWide or assumption-basedRecalculated from rehearsal evidenceReduces, but does not remove, uncertainty

Measure information value with your own planning model: reduced contingency reserve plus avoided rework value minus the live rehearsal fee. None of those terms is a LoloBuy promise. “Avoided rework” might mean not having to abandon an ineligible route after a final parcel is prepared. Use zero when the rehearsal result would not have changed any action.

Consider a fictional example in generic budget units. A planner holds a 40-unit shipping contingency because parcel height is unknown. The live rehearsal fee is F. After the result, current routes support a narrower range, allowing the planner to reduce the reserve by 18 units; the evidence also avoids a route-change task valued personally at 4 units. The planning value is 22 minus F. These figures explain the method only. They are not platform fees, prices or savings.

Know when rehearsal is likely to be worthwhile

Stronger case

The parcel combines irregular or bulky items; one dimension may decide route eligibility; several packing states produce materially different cost scenarios; or the remaining budget cannot tolerate a broad estimate.

Weaker case

The final item set is still changing; every current eligible route leads to the same decision; the fee exceeds the planning value; or the unresolved risk concerns customs, durability or delivery rather than package geometry.

Timing matters. Rehearsing too early can create a precise result for an incomplete item set. Waiting until all intended items and decision-changing QC questions are settled produces a cleaner comparison. At the same time, do not let a rehearsal request become an excuse to ignore seller or order deadlines unrelated to warehouse storage.

A split-parcel decision deserves two complete scenarios. Compare two packages with their own eligibility and costs against one consolidated package. Do not subtract one simulated carton from a guessed two-parcel total and call the difference a saving.

Reconcile rehearsal with the final outbound parcel

After the real parcel is prepared and weighed, add a final row. Record included items, packing services, actual weight, external dimensions, chargeable weight, selected route and final shipping charge. Keep the rehearsal row unchanged. The variance is useful only when both versions remain visible.

Audit in a fixed order: item set, packing instructions, actual weight, all three dimensions, route, billing standard, any displayed increment and currency. A one-centimetre carton change can matter when a route has a dimension gate; a route switch can change the billing rule; an added service can change both mass and shape. Find the first changed input before blaming the estimator.

Calculate simple variances: final actual weight minus rehearsal weight, each final dimension minus its rehearsal counterpart, and final charge minus the rehearsal-based estimate. Do not combine those into an accusation. The official interface already warns that the simulation may differ from actual outbound data. Use repeated records to improve future assumptions and raise a specific support question only when the current parcel remains unexplained.

Final decision checklist

  • The unresolved question is about packing, weight, dimensions, route eligibility or freight estimation.
  • The complete warehouse item set and selected packing instructions are frozen.
  • Draft weight, dimensions, route candidates and shipping range are saved.
  • The live rehearsal fee and currency are recorded at checkout.
  • The completed result is linked to the same item and instruction version.
  • Estimated weight and dimensions remain labelled as rehearsal evidence.
  • Routes are re-screened for current destination, item properties and limits.
  • Planning value is compared with the live fee using personal, stated assumptions.
  • A final outbound row preserves every variance instead of overwriting the simulation.
  • No rehearsal result is presented as guaranteed cost, time, eligibility or delivery.

LoloBuy rehearsal shipping is best understood as a paid information step between warehouse inventory and a real parcel. Its value is not a universal saving. Its value is a cleaner decision: better evidence about one defined packing scenario, a narrower budget range and a versioned record that can later be reconciled with the final weigh-in.

/guides/lolobuy-service-payment-fees-ver.title: LoloBuy Fees: Check Service, Payment and Shipping Costs
/guides/lolobuy-service-payment-fees-ver.description: Check LoloBuy product, service, payment and shipping charges in one cost record. Compare live totals without relying on outdated fee percentages.
/guides/lolobuy-service-payment-fees-ver.body:
Independent cost-audit guide

A trustworthy LoloBuy fee check does not begin with a percentage copied from a forum or an old guide. It begins with one current order, one selected currency, one payment method and the final amount shown before confirmation. Separate every cost line, calculate the effective difference and keep the result dated. If the screen does not identify a charge, label it unexplained rather than inventing a permanent service-fee rule.

Verified platform context: LoloBuy's public website was reachable on the fact-check date and continues to describe a product-link ordering flow followed by warehouse inspection and photographs. The public homepage does not provide one universal, complete fee table that can replace the live order and payment screens. No fixed service percentage, payment surcharge, exchange-rate markup, discount or refund deduction is claimed in this guide.

Separate the fee question into cost layers

“What are the LoloBuy fees?” is too broad to answer responsibly with one number. A reverse-shopping-agent order can contain the seller's product price, seller-to-warehouse delivery, a purchasing or service line, optional warehouse services, payment processing, currency conversion, later international freight and destination-side costs. Not every order shows every layer, and the same label may appear at a different step.

Begin with the transaction you are auditing. The first product payment and the later international parcel payment solve different problems. Do not divide a parcel fee by the product amount and call the result a purchasing service rate. Likewise, do not treat Chinese domestic delivery as a platform fee merely because it appears in the same total.

LayerEvidence to saveDo not rename it as
Seller priceSelected variant, quantity and current item amountAgent service fee
Domestic deliverySeller-to-warehouse charge shown for the orderInternational freight
Platform or optional serviceExact label, basis and order stagePayment fee
Payment and conversionCurrency, method, displayed charge and payable totalOne universal markup
International parcelPacked quote, route and current add-onsProduct-order cost

Capture a same-moment payment snapshot

A fee comparison fails when its inputs come from different times. Seller prices, exchange rates, discounts and payment options can move. Take the product-order subtotal and the final payable amount from the same checkout session, after the exact variant and quantity are selected. Record the date, time, account currency and payment method. If you change the method, save a second complete snapshot.

The snapshot should show the amount before payment without exposing private data. Keep product reference, item subtotal, domestic delivery, named service lines, discount, platform conversion if displayed, payment charge and final amount. Redact card digits, account balance, address and identity information. A screenshot without the currency or total cannot support a reliable calculation.

If the page updates after a payment method is selected, use the updated total. Do not compare the starting basket in one currency with a bank notification in another and attribute the entire difference to LoloBuy. Your bank or card provider can apply its own conversion or cross-border charge after the platform has shown its amount.

Calculate an effective difference without mislabelling it

First create an explained subtotal by adding the seller price, displayed domestic delivery and every named service or option. Then subtract any accepted discount. Compare that result with the platform's final payable amount in the same currency. The difference is an audit signal. It is not automatically a service fee because it may include rounding, payment processing or conversion.

For example, suppose a hypothetical order shows a 420-unit item subtotal, 18 units of domestic delivery and a named 6-unit optional service. The explained subtotal is 444 units. If the payable amount is 451 units, the unexplained difference is 7 units. The effective difference is 7 divided by 444, or about 1.58%. Those figures are a teaching example only; they are not current LoloBuy prices or rates.

Audit currency conversion as a separate decision

Identify the seller or order currency, the currency selected in the account, the platform amount displayed before confirmation and the currency your payment provider will actually debit. A public market rate is a reference, not the price a platform or bank must use. Timing, spread, processor rules and card terms can all produce a difference.

If the checkout lets you compare currencies without confirming payment, record each quote at nearly the same moment and use the same underlying order. Calculate the implied rate by dividing the payable amount by the source-currency total. Then compare payment methods on the final debit currency and total—not on a headline promise such as “no fee.” A method with no separate fee can still use a different conversion result.

Your bank statement belongs to another evidence layer. After payment, compare the platform confirmation with the amount actually debited. If they differ, check whether the bank identifies a foreign-transaction or conversion charge. Do not assign a provider charge to the shopping platform without evidence.

Compare payment methods on the same order

Hold the basket constant. Use the same product, quantity, domestic delivery, optional services, discount state and currency. Switch only the payment method, when the live interface permits a nonbinding comparison. Record availability, displayed fee, payable total, refund destination and any material term shown before confirmation. Do not assume that a method available to another country or account is available to yours.

A simple decision table needs five fields: method, debit currency, named processing charge, final payable amount and evidence timestamp. Add a note for provider-side charges that are not visible in the platform. If a method cannot be selected safely without initiating payment, do not manufacture a comparison. Report only the options you could observe.

  • Use one unchanged order as the baseline.
  • Record the currency at every step.
  • Separate named charges from calculated differences.
  • Keep discounts visible as reductions, not hidden inside a net rate.
  • Do not generalize one account, country or date to every buyer.

Keep optional services out of the payment-fee bucket

A warehouse service can be worth buying and still not be a payment fee. Record the exact service name, which item or parcel it applies to, when it is charged and whether the price is shown before confirmation. Examples might concern inspection, photos, measurements or packing, but this guide does not claim that any specific option is always available or priced at a fixed amount.

The same rule applies to international parcel add-ons. A packing or protection choice belongs to parcel planning, not to the purchasing-service rate. If a total changes after an option is added, preserve the before-and-after screens. This establishes the marginal cost of that selected option for that transaction without turning it into a permanent platform tariff.

Handle coupons and account credits transparently

A discount lowers the amount paid; it does not prove the underlying fee disappeared. Record the subtotal before the coupon, the accepted reduction and the total after it. Note the date and any eligibility text visible at checkout. Do not quote an advertised coupon value if the current order does not accept it, and do not subtract an expired promotion when comparing methods.

Account balance, promotional credit and cash payment are not necessarily equivalent. A balance may come from a prior refund or top-up, while a promotion may have restrictions. Keep source and value separate. If the checkout does not explain how a credit affects a future refund, do not promise an outcome.

Final fee-audit checklist

  1. Confirm the exact product variant, quantity and seller price.
  2. Record China domestic delivery as its own line.
  3. List every named platform or optional service.
  4. Apply discounts as separate reductions.
  5. Save account currency, debit currency and payment method.
  6. Compare the explained subtotal with the final payable amount.
  7. Label unexplained differences without guessing their cause.
  8. Check provider-side charges after payment separately.
  9. Date every claim and limit it to the observed transaction.
  10. Recheck the current screen before relying on an older guide.

The purpose of a LoloBuy service and payment fee audit is not to force every cost into one percentage. It is to make the transaction explainable. When each layer has a name, currency, evidence source and date, buyers can compare choices without turning a temporary checkout result into a platform-wide promise.

Evidence ledger and editorial limits

It was used only to confirm that the current public site remains accessible and describes product-link ordering plus warehouse inspection and photographs. The public homepage did not supply a complete universal fee schedule for this article.

/guides/lolobuy-shipping-calculator-esti.title: LoloBuy Shipping Calculator: Why the Estimate Can Change Before Final Billing
/guides/lolobuy-shipping-calculator-esti.description: Use the LoloBuy shipping calculator with defensible parcel inputs, compare estimates, and reconcile the result with final packed weight and billing.
/guides/lolobuy-shipping-calculator-esti.body:
Independent parcel-cost guide

A LoloBuy shipping estimate is useful when it answers a narrow planning question: what might a parcel with this destination, item type, weight and size cost through the options available now? It is not a locked quote for an unpacked haul. The reliable workflow is to record every input, compare only controlled scenarios and replace the estimate when final packed data becomes available.

Important boundary: the current LoloBuy estimator labels its freight result as a reference and says final cost is subject to actual billing. Its interface separates estimated shipping and chargeable weight from final shipping and final weight after weigh-in. Treat those labels as different stages, not as two names for one guaranteed amount.

What the LoloBuy shipping calculator can answer

The estimator can organize an early comparison. The current page asks for a destination and parcel information, then presents available-line information such as estimated freight, transit-time wording, weight or dimension limits and item eligibility where the relevant data is available. That helps a planner reject obviously unsuitable scenarios before warehouse packing.

It cannot know an item’s final carton, protective material, packing arrangement or verified outbound measurements before those facts exist. A seller’s stated weight may exclude packaging. A warehouse item record may describe one unit before consolidation. A trial calculation may use dimensions that came from a product listing rather than a packed parcel. Each can be useful, but each has a different confidence level.

Save the calculation date because routes, eligibility, price components and displayed conditions can change. Do not copy a route name or another buyer’s total into a permanent spreadsheet formula. Your evidence is the exact scenario you entered and the result returned at that time.

Audit five inputs before trusting the estimate

1. Destination

Use the actual receiving country or region shown by the live selector. A price seen for a different destination is not a comparable estimate. If the final address is undecided, calculate each real candidate separately and label the rows; do not average countries together.

2. Product category and properties

Choose the narrowest truthful item type. A generic clothing assumption is weak for an item with batteries, liquid, a magnetic component, fragile glass or another property that can affect route eligibility. Do not hide a sensitive attribute to force a result. If the current interface does not offer a defensible category, mark the estimate incomplete.

3. Weight

Record whether the number came from the seller, an individual warehouse record, your own comparable item or a final parcel weigh-in. Convert units once and retain the original. A guessed 2 kilograms should not later appear as a measured 2,000 grams simply because the units look more precise.

4. Length, width and height

Use external dimensions in the order requested by the page. Keep all three in the same unit and record whether they describe the bare product, retail box or packed parcel. Dimensions matter because some lines compare scale weight with a dimension-based billing weight or apply size limits. LoloBuy’s current interface exposes billing details by line; it does not justify one universal divisor for every option.

5. Assumed packaging

Name the packing state beside the calculator row: seller packaging, warehouse item, consolidated draft or final carton. If you assume box removal, compression, reinforcement or extra protection before the service is selected and completed, keep that as a scenario—not a fact.

InputLow-confidence evidenceHigher-confidence replacement
WeightSeller description or similar productWarehouse record, then final parcel weigh-in
DimensionsProduct or retail-box measurementsFinal external carton dimensions
Item typeBroad category guessRecorded warehouse property and live eligibility
RouteOld screenshot or community quoteCurrent result for the exact destination and parcel
PriceUn dated estimateDated final checkout amount and fee breakdown

Why the final charge can differ from the estimate

Packing changes physical data. Cartons, corner protection and cushioning add material. Removing unnecessary retail packaging can reduce space, while consolidating objects with incompatible shapes can create unused volume. The final parcel is therefore not always the sum of seller dimensions.

Chargeable weight can change. A line may use actual weight, dimension-based weight or the higher of the two, according to its current billing details. Entering weight without dimensions can hide this decision. Entering optimistic dimensions can create a false sense of precision.

Eligibility can change. The destination, product properties, weight band and size limits can remove an option that appeared in a generic estimate. One route-sensitive item can also change the choices for a consolidated parcel.

The checkout moment matters. Live pricing, discounts, tax treatment, declared services and route conditions can differ from an earlier planning session. Keep named charges separate so a change in packaging or route is not mistakenly blamed on currency conversion or payment fees.

Worked example: compare the assumption, not an invented rate

Imagine a planner has two accepted garments and one boxed accessory. The early worksheet uses a 2.4 kg total and external dimensions of 34 × 26 × 20 cm. Those figures are illustrative and do not represent LoloBuy data. Save the estimator result as Scenario A with its date, destination, chosen item properties and visible line conditions.

Now test Scenario B using the same destination and item properties but a carton of 40 × 30 × 24 cm. Keep the weight at 2.4 kg. If available options or estimated amounts change, the experiment shows that dimensions are decision-relevant. It does not prove the larger carton will be used. Scenario C can test 2.8 kg at the original dimensions to isolate weight sensitivity.

Controlled comparison: change one field per row. A useful sheet reads “same destination, category and dimensions; weight +0.4 kg.” A weak sheet changes country, weight, dimensions, packaging and route together, then cannot explain the difference.

Compare routes without ranking only the lowest estimate

After removing ineligible options, compare the evidence that affects your decision: estimated total, stated billing basis, weight and size limits, product eligibility, transit-time wording, tracking information and any current service terms. The lowest displayed number is not useful if the parcel cannot use that line.

Do not convert an estimated transit range into an arrival promise. The estimator’s purpose is cost and eligibility planning; carrier handoffs, customs processing and last-mile delivery happen later. Store time wording exactly as displayed and date it.

Use a decision rule before viewing results. For example: eliminate any line with unresolved item eligibility; eliminate any line whose limits are too close to low-confidence measurements; then compare the remaining estimated totals and documented conditions. This prevents a cheap first row from controlling the decision before important constraints are checked.

Replace the estimate with final parcel evidence

When packing closes, record the final scale weight, external dimensions, selected route, named services, discounts and total due. Put these beside the earlier calculator row instead of overwriting it. Calculate the absolute difference and percentage difference only after both values use the same currency.

Then explain the difference with evidence. “Final carton was 6 cm longer” is supportable. “The platform added a hidden markup” is not supportable unless a current fee line proves it. If the reason remains unknown, label it unresolved and retain the two records. The currency-conversion guide should be used only for exchange-rate effects, while the payment-fee guide keeps named transaction costs separate.

  1. Confirm every included item has a closed QC decision.
  2. Use the real destination and truthful item properties.
  3. Replace seller weight with warehouse and packed data when available.
  4. Record all three final external dimensions.
  5. Recheck current route eligibility and billing details.
  6. Save the final amount before payment and the charged amount afterward.
  7. Explain differences only with observable changes.
  8. Add the reconciled total to the landed-cost worksheet.
