/guides/lolobuy-total-landed-cost-worksh.title: LoloBuy Total Landed Cost: Build a Worksheet Before Shipping
/guides/lolobuy-total-landed-cost-worksh.description: Build a LoloBuy total landed cost worksheet that separates product, domestic freight, payment, warehouse, parcel and destination budget layers.
/guides/lolobuy-total-landed-cost-worksh.body:
LoloBuy's public homepage showed 180 days of free storage on 31 October 2026. Confirm the deadline and eligibility for each item in your account. Storage time does not extend a seller's return window.

Independent cost-planning guide

A LoloBuy total landed cost worksheet should answer one practical question: what will the order have cost when the parcel reaches you, not merely when the products are paid for? Separate the cost into six layers, record estimates as estimates, replace them with live account totals as each stage closes, and allocate shared parcel costs only after packed weight and dimensions are available.

What “total landed cost” should mean in your worksheet

Total landed cost is the sum of costs needed to move selected products from the seller stage through the warehouse and international parcel stage to the destination, plus any destination charges that actually apply. It is a planning total, not one universal number displayed at the moment you save a product link.

The distinction matters because different numbers become known at different times. A listing can show an item price before domestic seller-to-warehouse freight is final. A warehouse record can show an item after arrival but before it is packed with others. An international estimate can change when packed dimensions, route eligibility and current checkout terms are known. Destination taxes or carrier charges depend on the shipment and applicable rules.

Your worksheet therefore needs three states for every cell: estimate, live quoted and paid. Add the date and source beside each value. Never silently overwrite the estimate; retaining both numbers shows where the budget changed and makes the next order easier to plan.

Record six cost layers instead of one checkout total

1. Product cost

Use one row per exact product variant. Record the live product amount shown when the order is created, quantity, color, size or version, and the original product link. If the seller price changes before payment, update the paid column while preserving the earlier estimate. Do not treat a spreadsheet price or an old screenshot as a current quote.

2. Seller-to-warehouse freight

Domestic freight is the movement from the seller to the purchasing warehouse. Keep it separate from international shipping. When several items come from one seller, note whether the live order shows one combined domestic charge or item-level charges. Do not divide a shared charge equally unless that is the allocation rule you deliberately choose.

3. Payment and currency difference

Record the amount displayed before payment, the amount ultimately charged in your account currency, and any payment cost that is visibly itemized. The difference may reflect conversion, provider treatment or timing; the worksheet should document what occurred without inventing a platform markup. Check the live payment screen before authorizing the transaction.

4. Warehouse-stage choices

Record only optional services, packing choices or other amounts that are actually displayed for the order.

5. International parcel cost

This layer begins as a range, then becomes a live parcel quote, and finally a paid amount. Preserve actual packed weight, parcel dimensions, route name as displayed, packaging decisions and the quote date. Weight alone is not enough because billable weight can depend on dimensions and current route rules. Use the shipping cost preparation guide before accepting the final quote.

shipping cost preparation guide

6. Destination charges and delivery costs

Create a destination reserve rather than claiming a guaranteed tax-free or duty-free result. Research the current destination rules and carrier process for the shipment. Replace the reserve only when an actual tax, duty, handling or local-delivery charge appears. Legal thresholds and collection methods can change, so a previous parcel is evidence of that parcel—not a promise for the next one.

Build the worksheet with evidence beside every number

LayerEstimateLive or paidEvidence to save
ProductListing amountOrder paymentLink, variant, quantity, order record
Domestic freightSeller-stage estimateOrder amountSeller and shipment grouping
Payment / FXBudget bufferDisplayed and charged totalsDated payment summary
WarehouseOnly known choicesItemized live amountQC decision and selected option
International parcelPlanning rangeFinal live quotePacked weight, dimensions, route
DestinationResearched reserveActual chargeApplicable notice or receipt

Put an “unknown” marker in a cell that cannot yet be supported. Zero means you confirmed that the charge is zero; blank means the cost has not been checked. That small distinction prevents an incomplete total from looking final.

Add a confidence column. Product payments and completed domestic freight can be high-confidence. An unpacked parcel estimate should remain low-confidence. A destination reserve is a planning allowance until an applicable charge is known. The grand total should display both a current known total and a remaining range.

Calculation example: keep the arithmetic useful and the assumptions visible

Suppose a planning sheet contains three accepted items. To avoid suggesting current platform prices, the example uses fictional worksheet units, not a currency or LoloBuy fee schedule.

Illustrative calculation only: products 180 + 120 + 80 = 380 units; seller-to-warehouse freight 12 + 8 + 10 = 30; observed payment difference 9; an itemized warehouse choice 6; international parcel quote 150; destination reserve 40. The planning total is 380 + 30 + 9 + 6 + 150 + 40 = 615 units. If the destination reserve is not charged, the completed total becomes 575 units. If it is charged differently, replace the reserve with the actual amount.

The calculation is deliberately simple. Its value is the audit trail: every paid layer can be reconciled, while the one unresolved reserve remains visibly provisional. A worksheet that reports 615 as a guaranteed total would be misleading.

Allocate shared parcel costs without creating false precision

If you want a landed cost per item, shared parcel costs need an allocation rule. Equal division is easy but often distorts reality: a bulky jacket and a small accessory did not contribute equally to parcel size. Weight allocation is more defensible when item weights are available. Calculate each item's share as its weight divided by the combined item weight, then multiply that share by the shared international cost.

For example, if three items represent 50%, 30% and 20% of combined item weight, a 150-unit parcel charge can be allocated as 75, 45 and 30 units. Mark the method as editorial allocation; it is not necessarily how the carrier prices the parcel. When a rigid box or oversized shape drives dimensions, consider assigning a specific packaging or volume adjustment to that item instead.

Allocation supports decisions such as whether a low-priced accessory remains sensible inside a parcel. It should not be used to claim an exact standalone shipping price the item never received.

Use decision rules before adding, consolidating or shipping

  • Before paying: reject any row without an exact variant, current product amount and domestic-freight check.
  • At warehouse arrival: keep failed or unresolved QC items outside the parcel budget until the live order action is decided.
  • Before consolidation: compare compatible groups; one route-sensitive or bulky item may change the options for everything else.
  • At parcel quote: replace estimated shipping with packed weight, dimensions and the current route total.
  • Before dispatch: recheck recipient details, destination requirements and what the live checkout includes.
  • After delivery: reconcile actual destination charges and note why estimate and final total differed.

Free warehouse time can help items arrive at different dates before consolidation, but waiting is not automatically cheaper. Use the warehouse storage planning guide to set a personal decision date. A delayed low-value item should not hold an accepted parcel indefinitely merely because storage remains available.

warehouse storage planning guide

Keep cost and condition decisions connected. If QC photos reveal a meaningful mismatch, preserve the product link, selected variant, order record and relevant images before choosing the action shown for that order. The QC photo guide explains that evidence review. This worksheet does not promise a return, exchange or refund.

QC photo guide

Final landed-cost check before parcel submission

  1. Every selected item passed its recorded QC decision.
  2. Product and domestic-freight payments match the order records.
  3. Payment differences are observed values, not guessed percentages.
  4. Only visible, selected warehouse choices are included.
  5. Packed weight, dimensions and live international quote replace estimates.
  6. The destination reserve is labeled provisional until an actual charge exists.
  7. Shared costs use a stated, consistent allocation rule.
  8. The total shows its calculation date and remaining unknowns.

A useful LoloBuy cost worksheet is conservative: it exposes unknowns rather than hiding them inside one attractive number. That makes the sheet valuable before payment, at warehouse arrival, during consolidation and after delivery. The final total becomes a record you can learn from, while the next order still begins with fresh live evidence.

/guides/lolobuy-w2c-qc-shipping-2026.body:
Independent LoloBuy route guide

This article is an independent guide for buyers who use LoloBuyChina as a product discovery and route-planning page. Always verify live product prices, platform rules, service options and shipping quotes inside the official order flow before paying.

Why W2C Research Comes First

A good China shopping workflow does not begin with payment. It begins with understanding the product route. W2C means “where to cop,” but in practice it should mean more than a simple link. A useful W2C note explains what the item is, what category it belongs to, what product details are visible, and which information must still be verified before an order is placed.

LoloBuyChina works best when visitors use it as a starting point for product discovery rather than a final decision maker. A buyer may find shoes, clothing, accessories or electronic items through a spreadsheet-style page, but every route should still be checked for size, color, seller options, product availability and final price. This extra step reduces mistakes caused by broken links, unclear product photos or old listings.

How to Read QC Photos

QC photos are one of the most important checkpoints before international shipping. They help buyers review visible details after the item reaches a warehouse. QC is not a guarantee of authenticity, and it is not a replacement for product research, but it is useful for checking shape, color, stitching, labels, accessories, packaging and obvious defects.

Different product categories need different checks. For shoes, look at toe shape, heel height, pair balance, logo placement and sole details. For clothing, compare size tags, collar shape, print scale, stitching, measurements and fabric texture. For bags and accessories, check hardware, corners, zippers, straps, lining and included small parts. If an important detail is not visible, buyers should review whether extra photos or other inspection options are available in the current service panel.

Shipping Cost and Parcel Planning

International shipping is usually the part that surprises beginners. A product price alone does not represent the final cost. The landed cost can change after warehouse arrival because the parcel weight, volume, packaging style, destination and route selection all affect the final quote. A light item may still cost more if it is bulky, while a compact item may be easier to consolidate with other products.

Buyers should avoid choosing a shipping route only because it looks cheap at first glance. Route restrictions, delivery speed, product type and packaging choices matter. Shoes with boxes, electronics, batteries, liquids or fragile accessories can require extra attention. A safer workflow is to review QC photos first, decide whether to keep the item, then compare shipping options based on the final parcel information.

Using a Spreadsheet Method

A spreadsheet turns scattered product links into a manageable buying system. Useful columns include product name, category, W2C route, image reference, estimated price, size notes, QC notes, shipping concerns and final decision. This structure helps beginners understand what they are ordering and helps experienced buyers avoid repeating the same research.

The spreadsheet method also improves site navigation for visitors. Instead of browsing random products, users can move through a clearer path: discover an item, open the W2C source, review visible details, wait for QC photos, compare shipping choices and then decide whether the parcel is ready. This makes the buying journey more transparent and easier to explain.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

One common mistake is treating a product card as a final recommendation. A card should be a route, not a promise. Another mistake is ignoring QC photos because the product image looked good. Marketplace images, seller photos and warehouse photos may not always match perfectly. Buyers should also avoid forgetting about shipping weight, especially when ordering shoes, jackets or boxed items.

A better approach is slow and repeatable: save the W2C route, confirm the product details, review QC photos carefully, compare shipping options and keep notes for future purchases. LoloBuyChina can support this process by organizing product discovery and education, while the final order details should always be verified in the active platform workflow.

Conclusion

LoloBuy W2C research, QC photo checking and shipping preparation work best when they are connected into one clear process. A buyer who understands the route before ordering, reviews warehouse photos before shipping and plans parcel cost before submission is less likely to make avoidable mistakes. That is the purpose of a good guide page: not to rush a purchase, but to make every step easier to understand.

/guides/lolobuy-warehouse-storage-planni.title: LoloBuy Warehouse Storage Planning: Dates, QC and Parcel Decisions
/guides/lolobuy-warehouse-storage-planni.description: Plan LoloBuy warehouse storage with an arrival ledger, current account deadlines, QC decisions and compatible parcel groups.
/guides/lolobuy-warehouse-storage-planni.body:
LoloBuy's public homepage showed 180 days of free storage on 31 October 2026. Confirm the deadline and eligibility for each item in your account. Storage time does not extend a seller's return window.

Independent warehouse planning guide

The useful way to think about LoloBuy warehouse storage is as a scheduling tool. Record each item's arrival date, finish its QC decision promptly, group only compatible accepted items, and choose a personal parcel deadline well before the published storage limit. Storage can help stagger seller arrivals, but it is not a universal return period or a reason to postpone a mismatch.

Current planning rule: Confirm the storage deadline, any charge and available actions in your current account before scheduling a parcel. An older advertised storage period is not a current guarantee. Seller return windows must be checked separately.

Check the storage period attached to your current order

Use the storage deadline displayed for each received item. Products from different sellers may arrive on different dates, so keep an arrival ledger and confirm whether the current service allows them to wait for a combined parcel. Do not assume all items share one deadline or one fee arrangement.

Storage availability does not mean that every seller accepts returns for the same period, that all problems can wait, or that parcel packing is immediate. Seller action, warehouse storage and international processing are separate decisions. Check the current terms for each before relying on a deadline.

Use the confirmed account deadline as an outer boundary. Set an earlier working date with room for unresolved QC, another seller arrival, packing questions and the final parcel decision. If an extension or additional service is offered, confirm its conditions and cost before adding it to the plan.

Build an arrival ledger before the first package reaches the warehouse

A storage plan begins with one row per item, not one row per payment. Record the original product link, seller, exact variant, purchase date and expected domestic stage. When the item is marked received, add the warehouse arrival date shown in the order record. Keep the seller listing and selected option beside that date so later photos are compared with evidence instead of memory.

Add five decision fields: QC status, problem or question, action deadline shown in the current order, parcel group and personal ship-by date. Avoid writing only “good” or “bad.” A useful status is “identity matched; strap missing from available photos; targeted question open.” That wording explains what is complete and what still blocks acceptance.

  • Source URL and exact color, size, version or bundle
  • Warehouse arrival date from the current order record
  • QC state: pending, pass, focused question or action
  • Any live order deadline or seller condition displayed
  • Provisional parcel group and an earlier personal deadline

Keep this ledger private. It does not need passwords, payment details, a full address or tracking number. Its purpose is continuity across items and sellers, not a public order archive.

Finish QC decisions early instead of spending the storage window

LoloBuy's public workflow includes quality inspection and photographs when goods reach the warehouse. Review those images when the item arrives: confirm identity, selected variant, quantity, visible included pieces and meaningful condition. If one measurement or angle would change the decision, ask a focused question through whatever option is currently available rather than waiting for the rest of the haul.

A later parcel deadline cannot repair a missed seller action window. If a clear wrong color, size, model or damaged component appears, preserve the source listing, selected option, order record and relevant photo. Then check the live action available for that particular order. This article does not promise a return, exchange, refund, response time or fee because those depend on current terms, seller conditions, product and timing.

Accepted items can wait for a compatible group. Unresolved items should remain outside parcel selection. Marking those states separately prevents a buyer from submitting an entire group merely because most products look ready.

Group stored items by compatibility, not just arrival order

After QC, place each accepted item into a provisional group. Consider shape, fragility, packaging, product type and whether the item may affect available routes. Soft clothing and a rigid boxed item may need different protection. A battery, liquid, magnet or other route-sensitive category may need research before it joins ordinary goods. The live parcel interface and destination rules control eligibility.

LoloBuy publicly describes consolidating warehouse items, but consolidation is not proof that one parcel will always be cheaper or safer. A larger box may change billable volume, and one sensitive item can narrow the route list. Keep groups provisional until packed weight, dimensions and current route options are known.

A simple three-column decision works: ready and compatible; ready but route-sensitive; unresolved. The first column can form the main parcel candidate. Compare the second both inside and outside the group when live options are available. Never move the third into submission until its evidence question is closed.

Use a staged timeline with safety margins

Imagine item A arrives on day 1, item B on day 12 and item C on day 26. Item A passes QC immediately. Item B needs one size-label clarification and passes on day 14. Item C is a route-sensitive accessory. The correct question on day 26 is not “how many free days remain?” It is whether A and B should form a compatible parcel while C is checked separately.

Illustrative schedule, not a platform promise: days 1–3 review A; days 12–14 close B; day 26 research C; day 35 compare parcel groups; day 40 submit the chosen parcel. The numbers demonstrate a planning method only. Seller timing, warehouse processing, packing and route availability are live variables.

Set reminders from each item's own arrival date rather than from the first order payment. Use at least two internal checkpoints: a QC-complete target and a parcel-decision target. Leave a final margin that is meaningful for your circumstances instead of designing a plan that succeeds only if every late step is immediate.

Decide when waiting is useful and when it creates risk

Waiting is useful when a known compatible item is already on its way, the earlier goods have passed QC, and the combined parcel can be compared with split options before a comfortable personal deadline. Waiting is less useful when the later seller has no clear progress, an earlier item has an unresolved mismatch, or the possible addition could change route eligibility.

Use a stop rule. For example: if the later item has not reached the warehouse by the personal decision date, submit the ready group after checking current packing and route data. A stop rule prevents sunk-cost thinking, where one delayed low-value item holds several accepted products close to the storage boundary.

Run a final storage-to-parcel check

  1. Confirm every selected item has a recorded QC pass.
  2. Remove any item with an open question or live seller action.
  3. Review the oldest arrival date and current storage status.
  4. Check whether product types remain compatible with one route group.
  5. Choose packaging only after deciding what must be protected or retained.
  6. Use final packed weight and dimensions, not seller estimates.
  7. Recheck destination, recipient details and the live route terms.
  8. Save the parcel record with the item ledger and submission date.

Storage planning ends when the parcel decision becomes better supported by live evidence than continued waiting. The aim is not to use every available day. It is to turn staggered arrivals into orderly QC and consolidation decisions while preserving enough time to handle an unexpected problem.

Evidence ledger and editorial limits

The arrival ledger, three-group method, staged timeline and stop rule are independent LoloBuyChina editorial analysis. No fixed return rule, photo count, storage extension fee, route, packing duration, shipping price, delivery time or refund outcome is asserted.

Plan Lolobuy shipping by checking destination, actual and volumetric weight, route restrictions, packaging and the final checkout quote.

How to use this page

Shipping is not a fixed product price. Consolidation, parcel dimensions, destination and route eligibility can all change the final cost, so use the current platform quote before paying.

Check actual and volumetric weight

Use warehouse and packed-parcel data when available. Large boxes and bulky packaging can raise billable volume even when scale weight is moderate. Compare the parcel dimensions as well as the weight before selecting a route.

Confirm route eligibility

Available routes depend on the destination and item types. Batteries, liquids, fragile goods and other restricted categories can narrow the choices. Review the live route conditions for the exact parcel instead of relying on an older screenshot or another buyer’s quote.

Plan compatible consolidation

Group accepted items by protection and route compatibility, not only by arrival date. Consolidation may reduce repeated base charges, but a larger parcel is not automatically cheaper when dimensions increase volumetric weight.

Review packaging and checkout

Protective packaging can help fragile or shape-sensitive items, but it may add weight or volume. Confirm recipient details, packaging choices, the final live quote and current terms before submitting the parcel.

Build a complete shipping budget

LoloBuy FAQ

Practical answers for product research, inspection and parcel planning. Use your current account and order terms for transaction-specific conditions.

What is LoloBuyChina?

An independent product discovery and buying guide. It does not operate LoloBuy or process your orders.

What does W2C mean?

W2C means “where to cop”: the source product link or listing used to identify an item.

What does QC mean?

QC means quality check. In this guide, it refers to reviewing warehouse photos and available measurements before shipping.

Is a spreadsheet listing proof of stock?

No. Verify the current seller listing, selected variant and checkout. A saved card can outlive a product or price.

Where do product cards open?

Cards open their matching source catalogue records. Check the product reference and selected option on that page.

Why does an ID search show several items?

An unknown identifier opens catalogue search. Results are candidates; compare the source ID and product details before choosing.

Can I use Taobao, Weidian or 1688 links?

The finder recognises common product-link formats and checks established mappings. An unknown link opens search; platform import availability must be checked separately.

Why does a LoloBuy link fail?

Possible causes include an incomplete address, a source listing change, unavailable options or an import problem. Check the original source before retrying.

Where are my warehouse QC photos?

Look in the relevant item record in your current LoloBuy account. Match the order reference and selected variant before reviewing the images.

Can public QC photos prove my item is correct?

No. They describe another reference or inspection. Review the warehouse item assigned to your own order.

Do QC photos prove authenticity?

No. Photos can show visible details and requested measurements, but do not establish authenticity, hidden performance or long-term durability.

Does LoloBuy use US or UK shoe sizes?

The seller listing determines the size system. Check its chart and measurements; a size number alone does not identify US, UK or EU sizing.

How should I compare hoodie sizes?

Compare flat garment measurements with a hoodie that fits. Use the same chest-width, length and sleeve measurement method, not only S, M or L labels.

Is international shipping included in the product price?

Do not assume so. Record the item, domestic delivery, selected services and international parcel quote separately.

Why can the final shipping cost change?

Final packing, weight, dimensions, eligible routes and selected services can differ from an earlier estimate. Compare the same inputs and currency.

Is volumetric weight always charged?

Use the rule shown for the selected route. Some services use actual weight, others volume or the higher value; the divisor is not universal.

Does consolidation always save money?

No. Compare the complete quotes. Fewer parcels can reduce repeated base charges, but larger dimensions can increase billable weight.

Can every item travel on one route?

No. Check destination, item properties and current route restrictions, especially for batteries, liquids, fragile or bulky goods.

Does removing a shoe box always reduce cost?

No. The controlling weight or billing increment may stay the same. Compare the actual quote and the protection lost before removing packaging.

Does free storage extend a return deadline?

No. Storage and seller return conditions are separate. Check the deadline and eligibility shown for the exact order.

Can I cancel a paid order?

Check its current purchasing stage and available action. Obtain confirmation that the order is stopped; a message alone is not a completed cancellation.

Are all purchases returnable?

No. Eligibility depends on the item, seller, purchase channel and current terms. Manual or special purchases can have different conditions.

Is a balance credit the same as a bank refund?

No. Record the approved amount and destination. A platform balance credit and a refund to the original payment method are different outcomes.

Why does tracking say delivered before I receive the parcel?

Check whether the number belongs to seller-to-warehouse delivery or the international parcel. Domestic delivery to the warehouse is not delivery to your home.

Are coupon codes and reference prices guaranteed?

No. Check the live eligible transaction, expiry, currency and final payable amount. This site does not publish an unverified working coupon code.
